title.raw: 卷58 楊播 Volume 58: Yang Bo

sentences.zh: 楊播，字延慶，自云恒農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bo, styled Yanching, said of himself that he was a man of Huayin in Hengong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo, whose style name was Yanching, claimed to be a native of Huayin in Hengong commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖結，仕慕容氏，卒於中山相。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jie served the Murong clan and died as Minister of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jie had served the Murong and ended his career as chief minister of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珍，太祖時歸國，卒於上谷太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhen returned to the state in the time of Emperor Taizu and died as Administrator of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhen came over to the Wei during the reign of Emperor Daowu and died in office as Administrator of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖真，河內、清河二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of the two commanderies of Henei and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had served as Administrator of both Henei and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父懿，延興末為廣平太守，有稱績。

translations.literal: His father Yi, in the late Yanxing era served as Administrator of Guangping and had a reputation for achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi, late in the Yanxing period, served as Administrator of Guangping and won renown for his accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 高祖南巡，吏人頌之，加寧遠將軍，賜帛三百匹。

translations.literal: When the Emperor made a southern tour, officials and people praised him; he was promoted to General Pacifying the Distance and given three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: During a southern progress by Emperor Xiaowen, local officials and the populace lauded Yi; he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant and awarded three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 徵為選部給事中，有公平之譽。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant at the Department of Selection with a reputation for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as an attendant in the Selection Bureau, where he earned a name for impartiality.

sentences.zh: 除安南將軍、洛州刺史，未之任而卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Pacifying the South and Governor of Luozhou but died before taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Luozhou, but died before he could assume the office.

sentences.zh: 贈以本官，加弘農公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former office, with the additional title Duke of Hongnong, and was given the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted his former rank, ennobled as Duke of Hongnong, and given the posthumous epithet Jian, meaning Simple.

sentences.zh: 播本字元休，太和中，高祖賜改焉。

translations.literal: Bo's original style name was Yuanxiu; in the Taihe era the Emperor granted him the change.
translations.idiomatic: Bo had originally been styled Yuanxiu; during the Taihe reign period Emperor Xiaowen gave him the new style name Yanching.

sentences.zh: 母王氏，文明太后之外姑。

translations.literal: His mother, née Wang, was an aunt on the outside of Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Wang clan, was a maternal aunt of Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 播少修整，奉養盡禮。

translations.literal: Bo in youth was careful in self-cultivation and fulfilled ritual in supporting his parents.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bo was neat in deportment and punctilious in discharging his filial duties.

sentences.zh: 擢為中散，累遷給事，領中起部曹。

translations.literal: He was selected as Palace Attendant, repeatedly promoted to Attendant at the Office, and headed the Central Construction Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant, then successively to a post in the Secretariat, directing the central works bureau.

sentences.zh: 以外親，優賜亟加，前後萬計。

translations.literal: Because of his maternal connection, special gifts were repeatedly added, numbering in the tens of thousands in all.
translations.idiomatic: As a maternal relative of the throne, he received extraordinary largesse again and again, amounting to tens of thousands of pieces over the years.

sentences.zh: 進北部給事中。

translations.literal: He advanced to Attendant of the Northern Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Northern Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔播巡行北邊，高祖親送及戶，戒以軍略。

translations.literal: Bo was ordered to inspect the northern frontier; the Emperor personally escorted him to the door and instructed him on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was ordered to tour the northern border, Emperor Xiaowen saw him to the gate and briefed him on strategy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除龍驤將軍、員外常侍，轉衞尉少卿，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General Flying Dragon and Extraordinary Regular Attendant, then transferred to Vice-Director of the Court of Palace Guards, with his regular attendant status unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General Flying Dragon and supernumerary chamberlain, then Vice-Director of the Palace Guards while retaining his court attendant status.

sentences.zh: 與陽平王頤等出漠北擊蠕蠕，大獲而還。

translations.literal: With Prince Yangping Yi and others he marched beyond the desert to attack the Rouran and returned with great booty.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Yangping Yi and others he campaigned north of the desert against the Rouran and came back laden with spoils.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其勳，賜奴婢十口。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his merit and gave him ten male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen commended his achievement and granted him ten household slaves.

sentences.zh: 遷武衞將軍，復擊蠕蠕，至居然山而還。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Military Guards and again attacked the Rouran, returning as far as Juran Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Martial Guards and once more struck the Rouran, withdrawing only after reaching Juran Mountain.

sentences.zh: 除左將軍，尋假前將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left and soon given acting rank as General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left and shortly thereafter given acting rank as vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 隨車駕南討，至鍾離。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage on the southern campaign as far as Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern expedition as far as Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 師回，詔播領步卒三千、騎五百為眾軍殿。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Bo was ordered to command three thousand foot soldiers and five hundred horsemen as rearguard for the host.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal, Bo was ordered to take three thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry as rearguard for the entire army.

sentences.zh: 時春水初長，賊眾大至，舟艦塞川。

translations.literal: At that time the spring flood was rising; enemy forces arrived in great numbers and boats and ships choked the river.
translations.idiomatic: The spring floods were rising, and enemy forces came up in strength until boats and ships clogged the river.

sentences.zh: 播以諸軍渡淮未訖，嚴陳南岸，身自居後。

translations.literal: Because the various armies had not finished crossing the Huai, Bo drew up a strict formation on the south bank and himself took the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Since the main forces had not yet finished crossing the Huai, Bo drew up a tight formation on the south bank and placed himself at the rear.

sentences.zh: 諸軍渡盡，賊眾遂集，於是圍播。

translations.literal: When the armies had all crossed, the enemy forces gathered and thereupon surrounded Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armies had crossed, the enemy massed and surrounded Bo.

sentences.zh: 乃為圓陳以禦之，身自搏擊，斬殺甚多。

translations.literal: He then formed a circular battle array to resist them, personally joining the melee and killing many.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a circular defense and fought in the front ranks himself, killing a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 相拒再宿，軍人食盡，賊圍更急。

translations.literal: They faced each other for two nights; the soldiers' food was exhausted and the enemy siege grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted two days and nights; the troops ran out of provisions and the enemy ring drew tighter.

sentences.zh: 高祖在北而望之，既無舟船，不得救援。

translations.literal: The Emperor watched from the north bank; there were no boats and he could not send rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen watched from the north bank, but with no boats at hand he could not send relief.

sentences.zh: 水勢稍減，播領精騎三百歷其舟船，大呼曰：「今我欲渡，能戰者來。

translations.literal: When the water had subsided somewhat, Bo led three hundred picked horsemen through their boats and ships and shouted loudly, "I wish to cross now—let those who can fight come."
translations.idiomatic: As the flood eased, Bo led three hundred elite horsemen through the enemy fleet and shouted, "I am crossing now—whoever dares, come and fight!"

sentences.zh: 」賊莫敢動，遂擁眾而濟。

translations.literal: The enemy dared not move, and he thereupon led his troops across.
translations.idiomatic: None of the enemy stirred, and he brought his men safely across.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚壯之，賜爵華陰子，尋除右衞將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly admired his valor, ennobled him as Viscount of Huayin, and soon appointed him General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was deeply impressed and ennobled him as Viscount of Huayin; soon after he was appointed General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討崔慧景、蕭衍於鄧城，破之，進號平東將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the imperial carriage to attack Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan at Dengcheng, defeated them, and was advanced in title to General Pacifying the East.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied the emperor against Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan at Dengcheng, routed them, and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 時車駕耀威沔水，上巳設宴，高祖與中軍、彭城王勰賭射，左衞元遙在勰朋內，而播居帝曹。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage displayed its might on the Han River; on the Shangsi festival a banquet was held. The Emperor and the Central Army, Prince Pengcheng Xie, wagered at archery. Yuan Yao of the Left Guards was in Xie's party, while Bo was in the Emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was displaying its power on the Han River, an Upper Si festival banquet was held. Emperor Xiaowen and Prince Pengcheng Xie of the central army wagered at archery: Yuan Yao of the Left Guards was in Xie's party, Bo in the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 遙射侯正中，籌限已滿。

translations.literal: Yao shot and hit the target dead center; his tally of chips was already full.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's arrow struck the target squarely, filling his quota of scoring markers.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「左衞籌足，右衞不得不解。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The Left Guards' chips are full—the Right Guards cannot but be released from the wager."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Left Guards have met their tally—the Right Guards must now answer the challenge."

sentences.zh: 」播對曰：「仰恃聖恩，庶幾必爭。

translations.literal: Bo replied, "Relying on your sacred favor, I hope in all likelihood to contend."
translations.idiomatic: Bo replied, "With Your Majesty's grace behind me, I mean to try my best."

sentences.zh: 」於是彎弓而發，其箭正中。

translations.literal: He thereupon bent his bow and released; his arrow struck dead center.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his bow and loosed; the arrow struck the center of the target.

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「養由基之妙，何復過是。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "The skill of Yang Youji—how could it surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "The legendary Yang Youji could do no better than that."

sentences.zh: 」遂舉卮酒以賜播曰：「古人酒以養病，朕今賞卿之能，可謂今古之殊也。

translations.literal: He thereupon raised a cup of wine and bestowed it on Bo, saying, "The ancients used wine to nourish illness; I now reward your ability—truly a difference between past and present."
translations.idiomatic: He raised a cup of wine and gave it to Bo, saying, "In antiquity wine was taken as medicine; today I reward your skill—how the times have changed."

sentences.zh: 」從到懸瓠，除太府卿，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He followed to Xuancai, was appointed Director of the Imperial Storehouse, and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the court to Xuancai, was appointed Director of the Imperial Treasury, and was raised to the rank of marquis.

sentences.zh: 景明初，兼侍中，使恒州，贍恤寒乏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he served concurrently as Palace Attendant and was sent to Hengzhou to relieve and succor the cold and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era he served concurrently as Palace Attendant and was dispatched to Hengzhou to relieve the poor and needy.

sentences.zh: 轉左衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 出除安北將軍、并州刺史，固辭，乃授安西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Pacifying the North and Governor of Bingzhou; he firmly declined, and was then given General Pacifying the West and Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Bingzhou but firmly declined; he was then given General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Huazhou instead.

sentences.zh: 至州借民田，為御史王基所劾，削除官爵。

translations.literal: On reaching his province he borrowed fields from the people; he was impeached by the Censor Wang Ji and stripped of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he borrowed land from commoners; Censor Wang Ji impeached him and he was stripped of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年，卒于家。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanzhang he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanzhang he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子侃等停柩不葬，披訴積年，至熙平中乃贈鎮西將軍、雍州刺史，并復其爵，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: His son Kan and others kept the coffin unburied and petitioned for years; only in the Xiping era was he posthumously granted General Guarding the West and Governor of Yongzhou, and his rank was also restored, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan and others refused burial and petitioned year after year; only in the Xiping period was Bo posthumously made General Who Guards the West and Governor of Yongzhou, his titles restored, and the posthumous epithet Zhuang, meaning Stalwart, conferred.

sentences.zh: 侃，字士業。

translations.literal: Kan, styled Shiye.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, whose style name was Shiye.

sentences.zh: 頗愛琴書，尤好計畫。

translations.literal: He was quite fond of the zither and books and especially loved planning.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of music and books and had a particular gift for strategy.

sentences.zh: 時播一門，貴滿朝廷，兒姪早通，而侃獨不交遊，公卿罕有識者。

translations.literal: At that time Bo's whole clan was noble and filled the court; sons and nephews made early connections, but Kan alone did not associate with others, and few among the high ministers knew him.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yang clan of Bo's line filled the court with nobles, and his sons and nephews had wide connections early on; Kan alone kept to himself, and few grandees even knew who he was.

sentences.zh: 親朋勸其出仕，侃曰：「苟有良田，何憂晚歲，但恨無才具耳。」

translations.literal: Kin and friends urged him to enter office; Kan said, "If one has good fields, why worry about one's later years? I only regret lacking talent and ability."
translations.idiomatic: Relatives urged him to take office; Kan said, "With good land one need not fear old age—I only regret that I lack the talent for it."

sentences.zh: 年三十一，襲爵華陰伯。

translations.literal: At age thirty-one he inherited the rank of Marquis of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-one he inherited the marquisate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 釋褐太尉、汝南王悅騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: On first taking office he became Cavalry Adjutant to the Grand Marshal, Prince Runan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he became cavalry adjutant to Prince Runan Yue, Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史長孫稚請為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Governor of Yangzhou Zhangsun Zhi requested him as Recording Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Zhi, Governor of Yangzhou, asked that he serve as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍豫州刺史裴邃治合肥城，規相掩襲，密購壽春郭人李瓜花、袁建等令為內應。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Governor of Yuzhou Pei Sui fortified Hefei city, planning a converging surprise attack, and secretly bought Li Guahua, Yuan Jian, and others of the outer wards of Shouchun to serve as inside agents.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui, Xiao Yan's Governor of Yuzhou, fortified Hefei and planned a coordinated surprise attack, secretly recruiting Li Guahua, Yuan Jian, and others from the suburbs of Shouchun as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 邃已纂勒兵士，有期日矣，而慮壽春疑覺，遂謬移云：「魏始於馬頭置戍，如聞復欲修白捺舊城。

translations.literal: Sui had already mustered troops and set a date, but fearing that Shouchun might grow suspicious, he sent a false dispatch saying, "Wei has newly placed a garrison at Matou; I hear they also wish to repair the old city of Bainuo."
translations.idiomatic: Pei had already mustered his troops and fixed a date, but fearing Shouchun might suspect him, he sent a deceptive dispatch: "The Wei have newly garrisoned Matou, and I hear they mean to rebuild the old fort at Bainuo."

sentences.zh: 若爾，便稍相侵逼，此亦須營歐陽，設交境之備。

translations.literal: If so, there will gradually be mutual encroachment; this also requires fortifying Ouyang and establishing border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, our positions will gradually encroach on each other; we too must fortify Ouyang and prepare defenses along the border."

sentences.zh: 今板卒已集，唯聽信還。

translations.literal: The carpenters and soldiers are already assembled; I await only your reply to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: My laborers and troops are already assembled; I await only your word to stand down."

sentences.zh: 」佐僚咸欲以實答之，云無修白捺意。

translations.literal: The aides all wished to answer truthfully, saying there was no intention to repair Bainuo.
translations.idiomatic: The staff all wanted to reply honestly that there was no plan to rebuild Bainuo.

sentences.zh: 而侃曰：「白捺小城，本非形勝。

translations.literal: But Kan said, "Bainuo is a small city and in itself no strategic strongpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Bainuo is a minor post and no strategic prize in itself.

sentences.zh: 邃好小黠，今集兵遣移，虛搆是言，得無有別圖也？

translations.literal: Sui is fond of petty cunning; now he gathers troops and sends this dispatch—fabricating these words—could there not be another design?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei is clever in small ways; he has mustered troops and invented this story—surely he has some other design?"

sentences.zh: 」稚深悟之，乃云：「錄事可造移報。

translations.literal: Zhi deeply understood and said, "The Recording Secretary may draft the reply dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi saw through it at once and said, "Recording Secretary, draft the reply."

sentences.zh: 」侃移曰：「彼之纂兵，想別有意，何為妄構白捺也！

translations.literal: Kan's dispatch said, "His gathering of troops surely has another intent—why falsely fabricate Bainuo!"
translations.idiomatic: Kan's reply read: "Your mustering of troops surely serves some other purpose—why invent this tale about Bainuo!"

sentences.zh: 他人有心，予忖度之，勿謂秦無人也。

translations.literal: When another has a mind, I measure it—do not say Qin has no men.
translations.idiomatic: When another has designs, I can guess them—do not suppose that Qin has no worthy men."

sentences.zh: 」邃得移，謂已知覺，便爾散兵。

translations.literal: Sui received the dispatch, judged that he had been detected, and thereupon dispersed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pei received the reply, concluded he had been found out, and disbanded his forces.

sentences.zh: 瓜花等以期契不會，便相告發，伏辜者十數家。

translations.literal: Guahua and others, because the appointed rendezvous failed, informed on one another; more than ten households suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guahua and the others, their rendezvous having failed, turned informer on one another; more than ten households paid with their lives.

sentences.zh: 邃後竟襲壽春，入羅城而退。

translations.literal: Sui later actually raided Shouchun, entered the outer wall, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pei later did raid Shouchun, penetrated the outer wall, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遂列營於黎漿、梁城，日夕鈔掠。

translations.literal: He then set up camps at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided the countryside day and night.

sentences.zh: 稚乃奏侃為統軍。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon memorialized that Kan be made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then recommended Kan for command of the field army.

sentences.zh: 侃叔椿為雍州刺史，又請為其府錄事參軍，帶長安令，府州之務多所委決。

translations.literal: Kan's uncle Chun was Governor of Yongzhou and again requested him as Recording Adjutant of his headquarters, concurrently Magistrate of Chang'an; many matters of the prefecture and province were entrusted to his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's uncle Chun became Governor of Yongzhou and again took Kan on as recording secretary of his staff, with concurrent appointment as magistrate of Chang'an; Kan was entrusted with much of the province's business.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤等軍敗，北地功曹毛洪賓據郡引寇，抄掠渭北。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin and others' army was defeated, Mao Hongbin, Clerk of Merit of Beidi, seized the commandery and brought in invaders, raiding north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Baoyin's defeat, Mao Hongbin, merit clerk of Beidi commandery, seized the district and invited raiders, who plundered north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 侃啟椿自出討之。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized Chun to go out in person to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Kan urged Chun to take the field in person against them.

sentences.zh: 遂購募戰士，信宿之間得三千餘人，銜枚夜進，至馮翊郡西。

translations.literal: He then recruited fighting men; within a day and a night he obtained more than three thousand, advanced at night with gags in their mouths, and reached the west of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fighting men and within two days had more than three thousand; they marched by night with gags in their mouths and reached western Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 賊見大軍卒至，眾情離解，洪賓遂通書送質，乞求自效。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing the great army arrive suddenly, lost heart and scattered; Hongbin then sent a letter with hostages, begging to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, seeing the army appear so suddenly, lost heart; Hongbin sent letters and hostages offering to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是擒送宿勤明達兄子賊署南平王烏過仁。

translations.literal: He thereupon captured and sent Suqin Mingda's brother's son, the bandit-appointed Prince of Nanping Wuguo Ren.
translations.idiomatic: They captured and sent off Wuguo Ren, nephew of Suqin Mingda, whom the rebels had made Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 後雍州刺史蕭寶夤據州反，尚書僕射長孫稚討之，除侃鎮遠將軍、諫議大夫，為稚行臺左丞。

translations.literal: Later when Governor of Yongzhou Xiao Baoyin seized the province in rebellion, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Zhangsun Zhi campaigned against him; Kan was appointed General Guarding the Distance and Grand Master of Remonstrance, serving as Left Assistant of Zhi's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Governor Xiao Baoyin rebelled and held Yongzhou, Zhangsun Zhi, Vice Director of the Secretariat, marched against him; Kan was made General Who Guards the Distance and Grand Master of Remonstrance and served as left aide on Zhi's field staff.

sentences.zh: 尋轉通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Regular Attendant Direct and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Regular Attendant Direct and Upright.

sentences.zh: 軍次弘農，侃白稚曰：「昔魏武與韓遂、馬超挾關為壘，勝負之理，久而無決。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hongnong; Kan told Zhi, "Formerly Emperor Wu of Wei with Han Sui and Ma Chao held the Pass as a fortress—the principle of victory and defeat went long without decision."
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Hongnong, Kan told Zhi, "Long ago Cao Cao fought Han Sui and Ma Chao with the Pass as their fortress; victory and defeat hung in the balance for a long time."

sentences.zh: 豈才雄相類，算略抗行，當以河山險阻，難用智力。

translations.literal: Was it that their talents and heroism were alike and their stratagems matched? It should rather be that the rivers and mountains were perilous and steep, making intellect hard to employ.
translations.idiomatic: Was it because their talents were evenly matched and their stratagems equal? No—it was because the rivers and mountains were formidable and strategy alone could not decide the issue."

sentences.zh: 今賊守潼關，全據形勝，縱曹操更出，亦無所騁奇。

translations.literal: Now the rebels hold Tong Pass and fully occupy the strategic advantage; even if Cao Cao came forth again, there would be nowhere to display marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebels hold Tong Pass and occupy every advantage; even if Cao Cao himself returned, he could work no wonder there."

sentences.zh: 必須北取蒲坂，飛棹西岸，置兵死地，人有鬬心，華州之圍可不戰而解，潼關之賊必望風潰散。

translations.literal: One must take Puban in the north, send swift boats to the west bank, place troops in deadly ground so that men have fighting hearts—the siege of Huazhou can be lifted without battle, and the rebels at Tong Pass will surely scatter at the wind.
translations.idiomatic: We must seize Puban to the north, send swift boats to the west bank, and place our men where they must fight or die; then the siege of Huazhou will lift without a battle and the rebels at Tong Pass will break and flee."

sentences.zh: 諸處既平，長安自克。

translations.literal: When the various places are pacified, Chang'an will be taken of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Once the outlying positions are secured, Chang'an will fall of itself."

sentences.zh: 愚計可錄，請為明公前驅。

translations.literal: This foolish plan is worth recording; I beg to serve Your Excellency as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: This plan is sound, I believe; let me lead the way for you."

sentences.zh: 」稚曰：「薛脩義已圍河東，薛鳳賢又保安邑，都督宗正珍孫停師虞坂，久不能進，雖有此計，猶用為疑。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Xue Xiuyi has already besieged Hedong, Xue Fengxian again holds Anyi, and Commander Zongzheng Zhensun has halted his army at Yuban and long cannot advance; although there is this plan, I still harbor doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Xue Xiuyi already besieges Hedong, Xue Fengxian holds Anyi, and Commander Zongzheng Zhensun is stuck at Yuban and cannot advance; though your plan is good, I still hesitate."

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「珍孫本行陳一夫，因緣進達，可為人使，未可使人。

translations.literal: Kan said, "Zhensun was originally a common soldier of Chen, who rose through opportunity; he can be used by others but cannot use others.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Zhensun was originally a common soldier from Chen who rose by chance; others can command him, but he cannot command others.

sentences.zh: 一旦受元帥之任，處分三軍，精神亂矣，寧堪圍賊。

translations.literal: Once he receives a commander's commission and disposes the three armies, his spirit is in disorder—how could he bear to besiege rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Give him command of an army and his wits desert him—how can such a man besiege the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 河東治在蒲坂，西帶河湄，所部之民，多在東境。

translations.literal: Hedong's seat of government is at Puban, west along the river's edge; the people under its jurisdiction are mostly on the eastern border.
translations.idiomatic: The seat of Hedong is at Puban on the west bank; most of its people live on the east bank.

sentences.zh: 脩義驅率壯勇，西圍郡邑，父老妻弱，尚保舊村，若率眾一臨，方寸各亂，人人思歸，則郡圍自解。

translations.literal: Xiuyi drives and leads the stalwart and brave west to besiege the district towns; fathers, elders, wives, and children still hold to their old villages—if one leads the host there once, each heart will be in disorder, every man will think of returning, and the siege of the commandery will lift of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi has driven the able-bodied west to besiege the towns, leaving the old and weak in their villages; march there once and every household will panic, every man will want to go home, and the siege will collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 不戰而勝，昭然在目。

translations.literal: Victory without battle is clear before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Victory without fighting is plain to see."

sentences.zh: 」稚從之，令其子彥等領騎與侃於弘農北渡。

translations.literal: Zhi followed this advice and ordered his son Yan and others to lead cavalry with Kan to cross north of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi agreed and sent his son Yan with cavalry to cross the river north of Hongnong with Kan.

sentences.zh: 所領悉是騎士，習於野戰，未可攻城，便據石錐壁。

translations.literal: Those he led were all horsemen, skilled in field battle and unsuited to storming cities; they therefore seized Shizhui cliff.
translations.idiomatic: His force was all cavalry, trained for open battle and ill-suited to siege; they took position at Shizhui cliff.

sentences.zh: 侃乃班告曰：「今且停軍於此，以待步卒，兼觀民情向背，然後可行。

translations.literal: Kan then issued a proclamation saying, "For now halt the army here to await the foot soldiers, and meanwhile observe whether the people's hearts incline or turn away; then we may act."
translations.idiomatic: Kan then proclaimed, "We halt here to await the infantry and to see which way the people lean; only then will we move."

sentences.zh: 若送降名者，各自還村，候臺軍舉烽火，各亦應之，以明降款。

translations.literal: Those who submit names of surrender should each return to their villages; when the imperial army raises beacon fires, each should also respond to show intent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to surrender should return to their villages; when our army lights the beacon, each village that surrenders should answer with a fire of its own."

sentences.zh: 其無應烽者，即是不降之村，理須殄戮，賞賚軍士。

translations.literal: Those that do not answer the beacon are villages that do not surrender and should in principle be exterminated, with rewards given to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Villages that do not answer are villages that refuse surrender; they must be destroyed and the troops rewarded."

sentences.zh: 」民遂轉相告報，未實降者，亦詐舉烽，一宿之間，火光遍數百里內。

translations.literal: The people then told one another in turn; even those who had not truly surrendered also falsely raised beacons, and within one night fires blazed across several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread from village to village; even those who had not surrendered lit false beacon fires, and within a single night flames blazed across hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 圍城之寇，不測所以，各自散歸，脩義亦即逃遁。

translations.literal: The besieging bandits could not fathom the reason and each scattered homeward; Xiuyi also fled.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers could not understand what was happening and melted away; Xiuyi fled as well.

sentences.zh: 長安平，侃頗有力。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Kan had considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an was pacified, Kan had contributed substantially.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除冠軍將軍、東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was appointed General Champion and Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was made General Champion and Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年州罷，除中散大夫，為都督，鎮潼關。

translations.literal: That year the province was abolished; he was appointed Grand Master of Leisure and made Commander, garrisoning Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: That year the province was abolished; he was made Grand Master of Leisure and appointed commander to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除右將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed General of the Right and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made General of the Right and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬元顥內逼，詔以本官假撫軍將軍為都督，率眾鎮大梁，未發，詔行北中郎將。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, an edict appointed him in his former office with acting rank as General Who Pacifies the Army as Commander, to lead troops and garrison Daliang; before he set out, an edict made him acting Northern Central Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao threatened from within, Kan was ordered to keep his present rank while serving as acting Commander-in-Chief and General Who Pacifies the Army, to lead troops and hold Daliang; before he marched, he was made acting Northern Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 孝莊徙御河北，執侃手曰：「朕停卿蕃寄移任此者，正為今日。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang moved the imperial carriage to north of the Yellow River, took Kan's hand and said, "I kept you in your frontier post and transferred you here precisely for this day."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang withdrew north of the Yellow River, took Kan by the hand, and said, "I left you in your frontier post and then moved you here precisely for this moment."

sentences.zh: 但卿尊卑百口，若隨朕行，所累處大。

translations.literal: But your elders and juniors, a hundred mouths—if you follow me on the journey, the burden will be great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your whole clan, high and low, numbers a hundred souls; if you come with me, the risk to them will be great.

sentences.zh: 卿可還洛，寄之後圖。

translations.literal: You may return to Luoyang and entrust matters to later planning.
translations.idiomatic: Return to Luoyang and we will plan what comes next.

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「此誠陛下曲恩，寧可以臣微族，頓廢君臣之義。

translations.literal: Kan said, "This is truly Your Majesty's gracious bending of favor—how could I, for my humble clan, abruptly abandon the righteousness between ruler and minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Your Majesty's kindness is extraordinary, but how could I, for the sake of my humble clan, cast aside my duty to my sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 」固求陪從。

translations.literal: He firmly begged to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on accompanying the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至建州，敍行從功臣，自城陽王徽已下凡十人，並增三階。

translations.literal: On reaching Jianzhou, those who had followed on the journey were ranked for merit; from Prince Chengyang Hui downward there were ten in all, each raised three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianzhou the emperor rewarded those who had accompanied him on the flight; from Prince Chengyang Hui down, ten men in all were each raised three ranks.

sentences.zh: 以侃河梁之誠，特加四階。

translations.literal: Because of Kan's loyalty at the River Bridge, he was specially given four additional ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For Kan's loyalty at the River Bridge crossing, he was given four extra ranks.

sentences.zh: 侃固辭，乞同諸人，久乃見許。

translations.literal: Kan firmly declined and begged to be treated like the others; only after a long time was this permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kan declined and asked to be treated like the others; only after much persuasion was this allowed.

sentences.zh: 於是除鎮軍將軍、度支尚書、兼給事黃門侍郎，敷西縣開國公，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was then appointed General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Revenue Section, and concurrently Attendant at the Yellow Gate Office, ennobled as Duke of Fuxi county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Revenue Section, and concurrent Attendant of the Yellow Gate, ennobled as Duke of Fuxi with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南還，顥令蕭衍將陳慶之守北中城，自據南岸。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned south, Hao ordered Xiao Yan's general Chen Qingzhi to hold Beizhong city while he himself occupied the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned south, Yuan Hao left Xiao Yan's general Chen Qingzhi to hold Beizhong fortress while he himself held the south bank.

sentences.zh: 有夏州義士為顥守河中渚，乃密信通款，求破橋立效，尒朱榮率軍赴之。

translations.literal: A loyalist of Xiazhou was holding a mid-river islet for Hao and sent a secret letter offering allegiance, seeking to destroy the bridge and prove his merit; Erzhu Rong led an army to join him.
translations.idiomatic: A Xiazhou loyalist holding a mid-river islet for Yuan Hao sent secret word offering to defect and destroy the bridge; Erzhu Rong marched to support him.

sentences.zh: 及橋破，應接不果，皆為顥所屠滅。

translations.literal: When the bridge was broken, the link-up failed and all were slaughtered by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge was broken, but the rendezvous failed and Yuan Hao's forces slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 榮因悵然，將為還計，欲更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Rong therefore grew despondent and was about to plan a withdrawal, intending to scheme for a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was cast down and prepared to withdraw, planning to try again later.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「未審明大王發并州之日，已知有夏州義士指來相應，為欲廣申經略，寧復帝基乎？

translations.literal: Kan said, "I do not know whether when Your Illustrious Highness set out from Bingzhou you already knew that Xiazhou loyalists would come to join you, or whether you wished broadly to advance strategy and restore the imperial foundation?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "When Your Lordship left Bingzhou, did you already know that Xiazhou men would come to your aid, or did you mean to recover the empire by force of arms?"

sentences.zh: 夫兵散而更合，瘡愈而更戰，持此收功，自古不少，豈可以一圖不全，而眾慮頓廢。

translations.literal: Troops scatter and then reunite; wounds heal and one fights again—to hold to this and achieve success has not been rare since antiquity. How can one plan fail to succeed completely and all counsel be abruptly abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: Armies scatter and regroup, wounds heal and men fight again—victory on that basis is common enough in history. How can one setback end the whole enterprise?"

sentences.zh: 今事不果，乃是兩賊相殺，則大王之利矣。

translations.literal: Now that the affair has failed, it is two bandits killing each other—then it is to Your Lordship's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: This failure only means two enemies have destroyed each other—that works to your advantage.

sentences.zh: 若今即還，民情失望，去就之心，何由可保？

translations.literal: If you return now, the people's hearts will lose hope—how can their minds of going or staying be secured?
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw now and the people will lose heart; who will then stay loyal to you?"

sentences.zh: 未若召發民材，[1]惟多縛筏，間以舟楫，沿河廣布，令數百里中，皆為渡勢。

translations.literal: Better to summon and mobilize the people's timber, bind many rafts, intersperse boats and ships, and spread them widely along the river so that for several hundred li all appears as a crossing posture.
translations.idiomatic: Better to mobilize the populace, bind rafts in great numbers, mix in boats, and spread them along the river for hundreds of li so that everywhere looks like a crossing in the making."

sentences.zh: 首尾既遠，顥復知防何處，一旦得渡，必立大功。

translations.literal: With head and tail far apart, how will Hao know where to defend? Once a crossing is achieved, great merit is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Stretch the line far along the river and Yuan Hao will not know where to defend; cross once and you will win a great victory."

sentences.zh: 」榮大笑曰：「黃門即奏行此計。

translations.literal: Rong laughed greatly and said, "Yellow Gate, memorialize this plan at once for execution."
translations.idiomatic: Rong laughed and said, "Yellow Gate Attendant, submit that plan at once."

sentences.zh: 」於是尒朱兆與侃等遂與馬渚諸楊南渡，[2]破顥子領軍將軍冠受，擒之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erzhu Zhao with Kan and others crossed south with the Yangs of Mazhu, defeated Hao's son the General of the Van Guanshou, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao and Kan then crossed south with the Yang loyalists of Mazhu, defeated Yuan Hao's son Guanshou, commander of the van, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 顥便南走。

translations.literal: Hao thereupon fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao fled south.

sentences.zh: 車駕入都，侃解尚書，正黃門，加征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered the capital, Kan was relieved of the Ministry post, made regular Yellow Gate Attendant, and given additional rank as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the capital, Kan left the Ministry, became regular Yellow Gate Attendant, and was given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 以濟河之功，進爵濟北郡開國公，增邑五百戶，復除其長子師沖為祕書郎。

translations.literal: For the merit of crossing the river he was advanced to Duke of Jibei commandery with an added fief of five hundred households, and his eldest son Shichong was again appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: For crossing the river he was raised to Duke of Jibei with five hundred additional households in his fief, and his eldest son Shichong was appointed Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時所用錢，人多私鑄，稍就薄小，乃至風飄水浮，米斗幾直一千。

translations.literal: At that time the coin in use was largely privately cast by many people, gradually becoming thin and small, until it would float on wind or water; a dou of rice cost nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Coin in circulation was largely privately cast and grew ever thinner and lighter, until pieces would blow away in the wind or float on water; a dou of rice cost nearly a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 侃奏曰：「昔馬援至隴西，嘗上書求復五銖錢，事下三府，不許。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized, "Formerly when Ma Yuan reached Longxi he once submitted a memorial requesting restoration of the five-zhu coin; the matter was sent to the Three Offices and not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Kan memorialized, "Long ago, when Ma Yuan reached Longxi, he asked to restore the five-zhu coin; the Three Offices rejected the proposal."

sentences.zh: 及援徵入為虎賁中郎，親對光武申釋其趣，事始施行。

translations.literal: When Yuan was summoned in as Tiger-Fierce Central Commander he personally faced Emperor Guangwu and explained his intent, and only then was the matter put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was recalled as Tiger-Fierce Central Commander, he explained his reasoning to Emperor Guangwu in person, and only then was the reform adopted."

sentences.zh: 臣頃在雍州，亦表陳其事，聽人與官並鑄五銖錢，使人樂為，而俗弊得改。

translations.literal: Your servant recently in Yongzhou also memorialized on this matter, allowing people and the government jointly to cast five-zhu coin so that men would be glad to do it and popular abuses could be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in Yongzhou I memorialized on the same point, proposing that private persons and the government alike be allowed to cast five-zhu coins so that people would comply willingly and the currency abuse would end."

sentences.zh: 旨下尚書，八座不許。

translations.literal: The imperial directive went to the Ministry; the Eight Seats did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The order went to the Ministry, but the Eight Seats rejected it.

sentences.zh: 以今況昔，即理不殊。

translations.literal: Comparing the present with the past, the principle is not different.
translations.idiomatic: The present case is no different in principle from the past.

sentences.zh: 求取臣前表，經御披析。

translations.literal: I beg that my former memorial be retrieved and examined by Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that my earlier memorial be retrieved and considered by Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」侃乃隨事剖辨，孝莊從之，乃鑄五銖錢，如侃所奏。

translations.literal: Kan thereupon argued each point in turn; Emperor Xiaozhuang followed him and cast five-zhu coin as Kan had memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Kan argued each point in detail; Emperor Xiaozhuang agreed and ordered five-zhu coins cast as Kan had proposed.

sentences.zh: 万俟醜奴陷東秦，遂圍岐州，扇誘巴蜀。

translations.literal: Moqi Chounu seized Eastern Qin and thereupon besieged Qizhou, inciting Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Chounu overran Eastern Qin and besieged Qizhou, stirring up revolt in Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 大都督尒朱天光率眾西伐，詔侃以本官使持節、兼尚書僕射，為關右慰勞大使。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Erzhu Tianguang led troops west to campaign; Kan was ordered in his former office with Staff of Authority and concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat as Pacification and Comfort Commissioner for the Pass West.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Erzhu Tianguang marched west; Kan was ordered to keep his rank while serving with the Staff of Authority as concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat and commissioner to comfort the troops west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除侍中，加衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed Palace Attendant and given additional rank as General of the Guards and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made Palace Attendant with the additional titles General of the Guards and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 莊帝將圖尒朱榮也，侃與其內弟李晞、城陽王徽、侍中李彧等，咸預密謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was about to plot against Erzhu Rong, Kan with his wife's brother Li Xi, Prince Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Li Yu, and others all took part in the secret plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kan joined his brother-in-law Li Xi, Prince Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Li Yu, and others in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆之入洛也，侃時休沐，遂得潛竄，歸於華陰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was then on leave and was able to slip away secretly and return to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was on leave and managed to escape secretly to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，天光在關西，遣侃子婦父韋義遠招慰之，立盟許恕其罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, Tianguang was in the Pass West and sent Kan's son's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to summon and comfort him, establishing an oath and promising to pardon his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era, with Tianguang holding the west, he sent Kan's son's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to offer terms and swear to pardon Kan's offense.

sentences.zh: 侃從兄昱恐為家禍，令侃出應，假其食言，不過一人身歿，冀全百口。

translations.literal: Kan's cousin Yu feared disaster for the family and had Kan go out to answer the summons, counting on their breaking faith—no more than one man's death, hoping to preserve a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's cousin Yu, fearing for the clan, urged him to answer the summons, reckoning that if Tianguang broke his oath only one man would die and the rest of the family might be spared.

sentences.zh: 侃往赴之，秋七月，為天光所害。

translations.literal: Kan went to answer the call; in the seventh month of autumn he was killed by Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan went; in the seventh month Tianguang killed him.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Merit Equal to the Three Offices, and Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子純陀襲。

translations.literal: His son Chuntuo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuntuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 播弟椿，字延壽，本字仲考，太和中與播俱蒙高祖賜改。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Chun, styled Yanshou, originally styled Zhongkao; in the Taihe era he and Bo both received name changes from the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger brother Chun, styled Yanshou, had originally been styled Zhongkao; during the Taihe period he and Bo both received new names from Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 性寬謹，初拜中散，典御廐曹，以端慎小心，專司醫藥，遷內給事，與兄播並侍禁闈。

translations.literal: By nature broad and careful, on first appointment he was Palace Attendant and managed the Imperial Stables Section; for his upright caution he was put in charge of medicine, then transferred to Inner Attendant, serving the inner palace together with his brother Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature steady and cautious. On first appointment he was Palace Attendant in charge of the imperial stables; for his reliability he was put in charge of the medical service, then promoted to Inner Attendant, serving in the inner palace alongside his brother Bo.

sentences.zh: 又領蘭臺行職，改授中部曹，[3]析訟公正，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He also headed the provisional duties of the Orchid Terrace and was reassigned to the Central Section; he judged lawsuits fairly, and the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He also held provisional duties at the Orchid Terrace and was reassigned to the central bureau, where his fair adjudication won the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 及文明太后崩，高祖五日不食。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, the Emperor for five days took no food.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Xiaowen fasted for five days.

sentences.zh: 椿進諫曰：「陛下至性，孝過有虞，居哀五朝，水漿不御，羣下惶灼，莫知所言。

translations.literal: Chun advanced to remonstrate, saying, "Your Majesty's utmost nature—your filial piety surpasses that of Shun; you have dwelt in mourning for five mornings and taken neither water nor gruel; the hosts below are anxious and distressed, not knowing what to say."
translations.idiomatic: Chun remonstrated, "Your Majesty's filial devotion surpasses even that of Emperor Shun; for five days you have taken neither food nor drink, and your servants are beside themselves with fear."

sentences.zh: 陛下荷祖宗之業，臨萬國之重，豈可同匹夫之節，以取僵仆。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bears the enterprise of the ancestors and faces the weight of ten thousand states—how can you share the conduct of a common man and bring on collapse?
translations.idiomatic: You bear the legacy of your ancestors and the weight of the empire—how can you follow a commoner's mourning and risk collapse?"

sentences.zh: 且聖人之禮，毀不滅性，縱陛下欲自賢於萬代，其若宗廟何！

translations.literal: Moreover in the sages' ritual, mourning does not extinguish one's nature; even if Your Majesty wishes to make yourself more worthy than ten thousand generations, what of the ancestral temple!
translations.idiomatic: The sages taught that mourning must not destroy life itself; even if you wish to be praised by posterity, what will become of the ancestral temple?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖感其言，乃一進粥。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved by his words and thereupon took one serving of gruel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and took a bowl of gruel.

sentences.zh: 轉授宮輿曹少卿，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Vice-Director of the Imperial Carriages Section and given additional rank as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice-Director of the Imperial Carriages Section with the additional title Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為安遠將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖自洛向豫，幸其州館信宿，賜馬十匹、縑千匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor from Luoyang toward Yu visited his provincial residence for two nights and gave him ten horses and a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling from Luoyang toward Yu, Emperor Xiaowen stayed two nights at Chun's provincial residence and gave him ten horses and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Champion and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Champion and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖自鍾離趣鄴，至碻磝，[4]幸其州館，又賜馬二匹、縑千五百匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor from Zhongli toward Ye, reaching Que'ao, visited his provincial residence and again gave him two horses and fifteen hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On the march from Zhongli toward Ye, the emperor stopped at Que'ao, visited Chun's residence again, and gave him two more horses and fifteen hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 坐為平原太守崔敞所訟，廷尉論輒收市利，費用官炭，免官。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Administrator of Pingyuan Cui Chang; the Court of Justice judged that he repeatedly took market profits and used official charcoal, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Cui Chang of Pingyuan sued him; the Court of Justice found that he had repeatedly profited from market transactions and used official fuel, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後降為寧朔將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was demoted to General Pacifying the North and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later demoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，武興王楊集始為楊靈珍所破，降於蕭鸞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi had been defeated by Yang Lingzhen and submitted to Xiao Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Yang Jishi of Wuxing had been defeated by Yang Lingzhen and submitted to Xiao Luan of Qi.

sentences.zh: 至是，率賊萬餘自漢中而北，規復舊土。

translations.literal: At this time he led more than ten thousand bandits from Hanzhong northward, planning to recover his old territory.
translations.idiomatic: Now he led more than ten thousand followers north from Hanzhong, intending to recover his former lands.

sentences.zh: 椿領步騎五千出頓下辨，貽書集始，開以利害。

translations.literal: Chun led five thousand foot and horse troops out to encamp at Xiabian and sent Jishi a letter explaining advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Chun led five thousand infantry and cavalry to Xiabian and sent Jishi a letter setting out the costs and benefits of resistance.

sentences.zh: 集始執書對使者曰：「楊使君此書，除我心腹之疾。

translations.literal: Jishi took the letter and said to the envoy, "Commissioner Yang's letter removes the ailment of my heart and bowels."
translations.idiomatic: Jishi took the letter and told the envoy, "Commissioner Yang's letter has lifted the trouble from my heart."

sentences.zh: 」遂領其部曲千餘人來降。

translations.literal: He thereupon led more than a thousand of his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought more than a thousand of his followers in to surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老，解還。

translations.literal: Soon because his mother was old he was relieved and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was relieved of command and returned home because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 後武都氐楊會反，假椿節、冠軍將軍、都督西征諸軍事、行梁州刺史，與軍司羊祉討破之。

translations.literal: Later the Di of Wudu, Yang Hui, rebelled; Chun was given the Staff, rank as General Champion, command of all armies on the western expedition, and acting Governor of Liangzhou; with Army Supervisor Yang Zhi he defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Di chieftain Yang Hui of Wudu rebelled; Chun was given the Staff, the title General Champion, command of the western expedition, and acting governorship of Liangzhou; with Army Supervisor Yang Zhi he defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 於後梁州運糧，為羣氐劫奪，詔椿兼征虜將軍，持節招慰。

translations.literal: Afterward when Liangzhou transported grain it was plundered by Di bands; Chun was ordered concurrently as General Who Subdues the Barbarians with the Staff to summon and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when grain convoys from Liangzhou were raided by Di bands, Chun was ordered to serve concurrently as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and sent with the Staff to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 尋以氐叛，拜光祿大夫，假平西將軍，督征討諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: Soon because the Di rebelled he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and given acting rank as General Pacifying the West, supervising all punitive military affairs to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di rebelled again he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting General Who Pacifies the West, with overall command of the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 還，兼太僕卿。

translations.literal: On return he served concurrently as Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made concurrent Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 秦州羌呂苟兒、涇州屠各陳瞻等聚眾反，詔椿為別將，隸安西將軍元麗討之。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Qinzhou, Lü Gou'er, and the Tuyuhun of Jingzhou, Chen Zhan, and others gathered crowds in rebellion; Chun was ordered as separate commander under General Pacifying the West Yuan Li to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gou'er the Qiang of Qinzhou and Chen Zhan the Tuyuhun of Jingzhou rose in revolt; Chun was made a separate commander under General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Li.

sentences.zh: 賊入隴，守蹊自固。

translations.literal: The bandits entered Long and held the paths in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew into Long province and held the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 或謀伏兵山徑，斷其出入，待糧盡而攻之；

translations.literal: Some plotted to set ambush on the mountain paths, cut off their coming and going, and attack when grain was exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed ambushing the mountain paths, cutting off their supplies, and attacking when their food ran out;

sentences.zh: 或云斬除山木，縱火焚之，然後進討。

translations.literal: others said to cut down the mountain trees, set fire and burn them, and then advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: others proposed felling the trees, burning the slopes, and then advancing.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「並非計也。

translations.literal: Chun said, "Neither is a plan."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "Neither plan will do."

sentences.zh: 此本規盜，非有經略，自王師一至，無戰不摧，所以深竄者，正避死耳。

translations.literal: These are originally mere robbers without strategy; since the royal army arrived, no battle has failed to crush them—the reason they burrow deep is simply to avoid death.
translations.idiomatic: These are mere bandits without real strategy; since our army arrived they have lost every battle—they have gone to ground only to save their skins."

sentences.zh: 今宜勒三軍，勿更侵掠，賊必謂我見險不前，心輕我軍，然後掩其不備，可一舉而平矣。

translations.literal: Now one should order the three armies not to raid further; the bandits will surely think that seeing peril we do not advance and will despise our army in their hearts—then strike their unpreparedness and they can be pacified in one move.
translations.idiomatic: Order the army to cease raiding; the rebels will think we fear the terrain and despise us—then strike when they are off guard and we can finish them in one blow."

sentences.zh: 」乃緩師不進，賊果出掠，乃以軍中驢馬餌之，不加討逐。

translations.literal: He thereupon slowed the army and did not advance; the bandits indeed came out to raid, and he used the army's donkeys and horses as bait without pursuing.
translations.idiomatic: He held the army back; the rebels came out to raid, and he let them take the army's pack animals without pursuit.

sentences.zh: 如是多日，陰簡精卒，銜枚夜襲，斬瞻傳首。

translations.literal: After many such days he secretly selected elite troops, advanced at night with gags in their mouths, beheaded Zhan and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: After many days of this he secretly picked elite troops, attacked by night with gags in their mouths, killed Chen Zhan, and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 入正太僕卿，加安東將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as regular Director of the Imperial Stud and was given additional rank as General Pacifying the East.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as regular Director of the Imperial Stud and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 初，顯祖世有蠕蠕萬餘戶降附，居於高平、薄骨律二鎮，太和之末，叛走略盡，唯有一千餘家。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of Emperor Xianzu, more than ten thousand households of Rouran submitted and dwelt at the two garrisons of Gaoping and Boguli; at the end of Taihe most rebelled and fled, leaving only a little more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the reign of Emperor Xianzu, more than ten thousand Rouran households had submitted and been settled at the garrisons of Gaoping and Boguli; by the end of Taihe most had fled, and only a little over a thousand households remained.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫王通、高平鎮將郎育等，求徙置淮北，防其叛走。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Palace Counsel Wang Tong, Garrison Commander of Gaoping Lang Yu, and others requested relocation north of the Huai to guard against their fleeing in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, Lang Yu, commander of Gaoping garrison, and others asked that the remnant be moved north of the Huai to prevent further defection.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，慮不從命，乃使椿持節往徙焉。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it; fearing they would not obey orders, Chun was sent with the Staff to relocate them.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved, but fearing resistance sent Chun with the Staff to carry out the relocation.

sentences.zh: 椿以為徙之無益，上書曰：「臣以古人有言：裔不謀夏，夷不亂華。

translations.literal: Chun thought relocation would be of no benefit and submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant considers that the ancients had a saying: outsiders do not plot against the Central States, barbarians do not disturb the Hua."
translations.idiomatic: Chun argued that relocation would do no good and memorialized, "The ancients said that outsiders should not meddle in the affairs of the Central States, nor barbarians disturb the civilized realm."

sentences.zh: 荒忽之人，覊縻而已。

translations.literal: Wild and heedless people are only to be bridled and tethered.
translations.idiomatic: Such wild peoples are fit only to be kept on loose reins.

sentences.zh: 是以先朝居之於荒服之間者，正欲悅近來遠，招附殊俗，亦以別華戎、異內外也。

translations.literal: Therefore the former court placed them among the wild borderlands precisely to please those near and draw those far, to recruit and attach foreign customs, and also to distinguish Hua from Rong and separate inner from outer.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the former court settled them on the frontier—to draw the near and win the far, to attach foreign peoples, and to mark the line between Chinese and barbarian, inner and outer.

sentences.zh: 今新附者眾，若舊者見徙，新者必不安。

translations.literal: Now the newly submitted are many; if the old are seen relocated, the new will surely be uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Many new submitters have lately arrived; if the older groups are moved, the newcomers will grow uneasy.

sentences.zh: 不安必思土，思土則走叛。

translations.literal: Unease will surely bring thoughts of home; thoughts of home will bring flight and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Unease breeds homesickness, and homesickness breeds defection.

sentences.zh: 狐死首丘，其害方甚。

translations.literal: When the fox dies its head faces its mound—the harm will be very great.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, the fox turns its head toward its mound at death—the harm will be grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 又此族類，衣毛食肉，樂冬便寒。

translations.literal: Moreover this race wears fur and eats meat, delights in winter and finds cold convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover these people wear furs and eat meat; they thrive in cold and suffer in heat.

sentences.zh: 南土濕熱，往必將盡。

translations.literal: The southern lands are damp and hot; if they go there they will surely perish.
translations.idiomatic: The south is damp and hot; move them there and they will perish.

sentences.zh: 進失歸伏之心，退非藩衞之益。

translations.literal: Advancing loses the hearts of those who submit; retreating is no benefit to frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: We would lose their loyalty and gain nothing for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 徙在中夏，而生後患，愚心所見，謂為不可。

translations.literal: To relocate them into the Central States and breed later calamity—in this foolish heart's view it is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To move them into the heartland and breed future trouble is, in my view, unwise."

sentences.zh: 」時八座議不從，遂徙於濟州緣河居之。

translations.literal: At that time the Eight Seats deliberated and did not follow him; they thereupon relocated them to Jizhou to dwell along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats rejected his advice and settled the Rouran along the river in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 冀州元愉之難，果悉浮河赴賊，所在鈔掠，如椿所策。

translations.literal: At the trouble of Yuan Yu in Jizhou, they indeed all crossed the river by raft to join the rebels and raided wherever they were, as Chun had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuan Yu's rebellion in Jizhou they crossed the river to join the rebels and raided the countryside, exactly as Chun had predicted.

sentences.zh: 永平初，徐州城人成景儁以宿預叛，詔椿率眾四萬討之，不克而返。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping, Cheng Jingjun of Xuzhou city rebelled with Suyu; an edict ordered Chun to lead forty thousand to campaign against him; he did not overcome them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongping, Cheng Jingjun of Xuzhou rebelled and seized Suyu; Chun was ordered to lead forty thousand men against him but failed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 久之，除都督朔州撫冥武川懷朔三鎮三道諸軍事、平北將軍、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Commander of all military affairs of the three routes of the three garrisons of Shuozhou, Fuming, Wuchuan, and Huaishuo, General Pacifying the North, and Governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made commander of the three northern garrison routes of Shuozhou, Fuming, Wuchuan, and Huaishuo, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 在州，為廷尉奏椿前為太僕卿日，招引細人，盜種牧田三百四十頃，依律處刑五歲。

translations.literal: While in the province, the Court of Justice memorialized that in Chun's former days as Director of the Imperial Stud he had recruited petty men and illicitly planted three hundred forty qing of pasture land; according to law he was sentenced to five years.
translations.idiomatic: While in office the Court of Justice reported that during Chun's tenure as Director of the Imperial Stud he had recruited commoners to plant three hundred forty qing of pasture land illegally; by law he was sentenced to five years' penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 尚書邢巒，據正始別格奏椿罪應除名為庶人，注籍盜門，同籍合門不仕。

translations.literal: Director Xing Luan, citing the Zhengshi supplementary statutes, memorialized that Chun's crime warranted removal of name and reduction to commoner status, registration in the robber gate, and that those of the same register in the same gate should not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xing Luan, citing the Zhengshi supplementary statutes, argued that Chun should be struck from the rolls, reduced to commoner status, and registered in the robber category, barring his entire household from office.

sentences.zh: 世宗以新律既班，不宜雜用舊制，詔依寺斷，聽以贖論。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because the new code had been promulgated and old regulations should not be mixed in use, ordered that the Court's judgment be followed and redemption be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong held that with the new code in force the old statutes should not apply; he ordered the Court's judgment followed and allowed Chun to redeem his sentence.

sentences.zh: 尋加撫軍將軍，入除都官尚書，監修白溝堤堰。

translations.literal: Soon he was given additional rank as General Who Pacifies the Army, entered court as Director of the Capital Offices, and supervised repair of the Baigou dikes and weirs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the Army, recalled as Director of the Capital Offices, and put in charge of repairing the Baigou dikes.

sentences.zh: 復以本將軍除定州刺史。

translations.literal: Again with his former general's rank he was appointed Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Governor of Dingzhou while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 自太祖平中山，多置軍府，以相威攝。

translations.literal: Since the Taizu pacified Zhongshan, many army offices were established to intimidate and control one another.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizu conquered Zhongshan, the court established numerous army offices to keep one another in check.

sentences.zh: 凡有八軍，軍各配兵五千，食祿主帥軍各四十六人。

translations.literal: In all there were eight armies; each army was allotted five thousand soldiers; salary-receiving commanders numbered forty-six per army.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight armies in all, each with five thousand troops and forty-six salaried commanders.

sentences.zh: 自中原稍定，八軍之兵，漸割南戍，一軍兵纔千餘，然主帥如故，費祿不少。

translations.literal: Since the Central Plains were gradually settled, the troops of the eight armies were progressively reassigned to southern garrisons; one army had barely more than a thousand soldiers, yet the commanders remained as before, and salary expenses were not small.
translations.idiomatic: As the Central Plains grew more secure, troops from the eight armies were gradually shifted to southern garrisons until each army had barely a thousand men, while the full complement of commanders remained on the payroll.

sentences.zh: 椿表罷四軍，減其帥百八十四人。

translations.literal: Chun memorialized to abolish four armies and reduce their commanders by one hundred eighty-four men.
translations.idiomatic: Chun submitted a memorial proposing to disband four armies and cut one hundred eighty-four commanders.

sentences.zh: 州有宗子稻田，屯兵八百戶，年常發夫三千，草三百車，修補畦堰。

translations.literal: The province had imperial clan rice fields; eight hundred garrison households were stationed there; each year three thousand corvée laborers were dispatched, three hundred cartloads of fodder, to repair the field dikes and weirs.
translations.idiomatic: The province maintained imperial clan rice fields worked by eight hundred garrison households; every year three thousand corvée laborers and three hundred cartloads of fodder were levied to repair the dikes and irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 椿以屯兵惟輸此田課，更無徭役，及至閑月，即應修治，不容復勞百姓，椿亦表罷。

translations.literal: Chun argued that the garrison troops paid only the tax on these fields and had no other corvée duties; when the slack months came they ought to do the repairs themselves, and the common people should not be burdened again. Chun also memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Chun argued that the garrison troops owed only the field tax and no other corvée service, and that in slack seasons they should handle repairs themselves rather than burden the populace again; he memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 椿在州，因治黑山道餘功，伐木私造佛寺，役使兵力，為御史所劾，除名為庶人。

translations.literal: While Chun was in the province, using leftover labor from repairing the Heishan road, he cut timber to build a Buddhist temple privately and employed soldiers; he was impeached by the censor and stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as governor, Chun used leftover labor from the Heishan road project to cut timber and build a private Buddhist temple, employing soldiers in the work; the censor impeached him, and he was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，除輔國將軍、南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengguang he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時南秦州反叛，路又阻塞，仍停長安。

translations.literal: At that time Southern Qinzhou had rebelled and the roads were blocked; he therefore remained at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qinzhou was in rebellion and the roads were impassable, so he remained at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 轉授岐州，復除撫軍將軍、衞尉卿。

translations.literal: The appointment was transferred to Qizhou; he was again appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The post was reassigned to Qizhou, and he was again made General Who Pacifies the Army and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 轉左衞將軍，又兼尚書右僕射，馳驛詣并肆，齎絹三萬匹，募召恒朔流民，揀充軍士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard, and additionally served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he rushed by post relay to Bing and Si, carrying thirty thousand bolts of silk to recruit and summon displaced people from Heng and Shuo and select them to fill out the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left Guard and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then dispatched by post relay to Bingzhou with thirty thousand bolts of silk to recruit displaced people from the Heng and Shuo region and draft them as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 不行。

translations.literal: He did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋加衞將軍，出除都督雍南豳二州諸軍事、本將軍、雍州刺史，又進號車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was given additional rank as General of the Guard; he went out and was appointed Commander of all military affairs of Yong, Southern Bin, and the two provinces, with his former general's rank and as Governor of Yongzhou; he was further promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with the Three Precedence of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General of the Guard and sent out as commander of military affairs in Yongzhou and Southern Binzhou, Governor of Yongzhou, and then promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with the Three Precedence of Honor.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤、元恒芝諸軍為賊所敗，恒芝從渭北東渡，椿使追之，不止。

translations.literal: The armies of Xiao Baoyin, Yuan Hengzhi, and others were defeated by the rebels; Hengzhi crossed east from the north bank of the Wei; Chun sent men to pursue him, but he did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Xiao Baoyin, Yuan Hengzhi, and others were routed by the rebels; Hengzhi fled east across the Wei from its north bank, and though Chun sent pursuers after him, he would not halt.

sentences.zh: 寶夤後至，留於逍遙園內，收集將士，猶得萬餘，由是三輔人心，頗得安帖。

translations.literal: Baoyin arrived later and remained in Xiaoyao Garden, gathering officers and soldiers; he still mustered more than ten thousand; thereby the hearts of the people in the Three Adjuncts were somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin arrived afterward and took refuge in Xiaoyao Garden, where he gathered officers and soldiers until he still had more than ten thousand men; this helped steady public morale in the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 于時，涇岐及豳悉已陷賊，扶風以西，非復國有。

translations.literal: At that time Jing, Qi, and Bin had all fallen to the rebels; west of Fufeng was no longer territory of the state.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jingzhou, Qizhou, and Binzhou had all fallen to the rebels, and everything west of Fufeng was lost to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 椿乃鳩募內外，得七千餘人，遣兄子錄事參軍侃率以防禦。

translations.literal: Chun thereupon gathered recruits inside and outside the city, obtaining more than seven thousand men, and sent his elder brother's son, the record-keeping staff officer Kan, to lead them in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chun then raised more than seven thousand men from inside and outside the city and sent his nephew Kan, a record-keeping staff officer, to lead them in defense.

sentences.zh: 詔椿以本官加侍中、兼尚書右僕射為行臺，節度關西諸將，其統內五品已下、郡縣須有補用者，任即擬授。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chun, with his former office plus Palace Attendant and concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, as mobile headquarters, to command the generals west of the passes; within his jurisdiction, for fifth rank and below and for counties and commanderies needing appointments, he was empowered to propose and confer them at once.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Chun mobile headquarters commander with his existing titles plus Palace Attendant and concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, giving him authority over the generals west of the passes and the power to appoint officials of fifth rank and below throughout his jurisdiction as needed.

sentences.zh: 椿遇暴疾，頻啟乞解。

translations.literal: Chun suffered a sudden severe illness and repeatedly memorialized begging to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Chun fell gravely ill and repeatedly petitioned to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，以蕭寶夤代椿為刺史、行臺。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it; Xiao Baoyin was appointed to replace Chun as governor and mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request and replaced him with Xiao Baoyin as governor and mobile headquarters commander.

sentences.zh: 椿還鄉里，遇子昱將還京師，因謂曰：「當今雍州刺史亦不賢於蕭寶夤，[5]但其上佐，朝廷應遣心膂重人，何得任其牒用？

translations.literal: Chun returned to his home district and met his son Yu, who was about to return to the capital; he therefore said to him: "The present Governor of Yongzhou is no more worthy than Xiao Baoyin, [5] but as for his senior aides, the court ought to send men of utmost trust and weight—how can he be allowed to appoint whomever he lists?
translations.idiomatic: On returning home Chun met his son Yu, who was heading back to the capital, and said to him: "The current Governor of Yongzhou is no better than Xiao Baoyin, [5] but for his senior staff the court should send men it truly trusts. How can he be allowed to appoint whomever he chooses?

sentences.zh: 此乃聖朝百慮之一失。

translations.literal: This is one lapse among the myriad considerations of the sacred court.
translations.idiomatic: That is one mistake among the court's many deliberations.

sentences.zh: 且寶夤不藉刺史為榮，吾觀其得州，喜悅不少，至於賞罰云為，不依常憲，恐有異心。

translations.literal: Moreover Baoyin does not rely on the governorship for honor; I observe that upon receiving the province his joy was not small; as for rewards, punishments, and conduct, he does not follow the usual statutes—I fear he harbors ulterior intent.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Baoyin does not need the governorship for prestige, yet I saw how pleased he was to receive the post; his rewards, punishments, and conduct do not follow regular law, and I fear he has ulterior motives.

sentences.zh: 關中可惜。

translations.literal: Guangzhong is a pity.
translations.idiomatic: It would be a tragedy to lose Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 汝今赴京，稱吾此意，以啟二聖，并白宰輔，更遣長史、司馬、防城都督。

translations.literal: You now go to the capital; speak this intention of mine, report it to the Two Sovereigns, and also inform the chief ministers to send anew a chief clerk, a marshal, and a city-defense commander.
translations.idiomatic: When you reach the capital, convey my views to the Two Sovereigns and inform the chief ministers that they should send a chief clerk, a marshal, and a city-defense commander.

sentences.zh: 欲安關中，正須三人耳。

translations.literal: To secure Guanzhong, precisely three men are needed.
translations.idiomatic: Securing Guanzhong requires only these three men.

sentences.zh: 如其不遣，必成深憂。

translations.literal: If they are not sent, deep worry will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not sent, grave trouble will follow.

sentences.zh: 」昱還，面啟肅宗及靈太后，並不信納。

translations.literal: Yu returned and reported face to face to Emperor Suzong and Empress Dowager Ling; neither believed or accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu returned and reported Chun's warning directly to Emperor Suzong and Empress Dowager Ling, but neither believed him.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤邀害御史中尉酈道元，猶上表自理，稱為椿父子所謗。

translations.literal: When Baoyin lured and killed the Censor-in-Chief Li Daoyuan, he still submitted a memorial in self-defense, saying he had been slandered by Chun and his son.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin ambushed and killed Censor-in-Chief Li Daoyuan, he still submitted a memorial in his own defense, claiming he had been slandered by Chun and his son.

sentences.zh: 詔復除椿都督雍岐南豳三州諸軍事、本將軍、開府儀同三司、雍州刺史、討蜀大都督。

translations.literal: An edict again appointed Chun Commander of all military affairs of Yong, Qi, Southern Bin, and the three provinces, with his former general's rank, Grand General with the Three Precedence of Honor and an open office, Governor of Yongzhou, and Grand Commander for the Campaign against Shu.
