translations.idiomatic: An edict reappointed Chun commander of military affairs in Yongzhou, Qizhou, and Southern Binzhou, Governor of Yongzhou, Grand General with the Three Precedence of Honor and an open office, and Grand Commander for the Campaign against Shu.

sentences.zh: 椿辭以老病，不行。

translations.literal: Chun declined on grounds of old age and illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Chun declined on grounds of age and illness and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 建義元年，遷司徒公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi he was transferred to Duke of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyi he was made Duke of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮東討葛榮，詔椿統眾為後軍，榮擒葛榮，乃止。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong campaigned east against Ge Rong; an edict ordered Chun to command the troops as rear guard; when Rong captured Ge Rong, he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched east against Ge Rong, Chun was ordered to command the rear guard; he halted once Rong captured Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 永安初，進位太保、侍中，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was promoted to Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and granted rear guard musical accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yong'an he was promoted to Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and granted the honor of rear guard musical accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，椿子征東將軍昱出鎮滎陽，為顥所擒。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu, General Who Conquers the East, went out to garrison Xingyang and was captured by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu, General Who Conquers the East, was garrisoning Xingyang and was captured by Hao.

sentences.zh: 又椿弟順為冀州刺史，順子仲宣正平太守，兄子侃、弟子遁並從駕河北，為顥嫌疑。

translations.literal: Moreover Chun's younger brother Shun was Governor of Jizhou; Shun's son Zhongxuan was Administrator of Zhengping; Chun's elder brother's son Kan and younger brother's son Dun all followed the imperial carriage north of the Yellow River and were suspected by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Shun was Governor of Jizhou; Shun's son Zhongxuan was Administrator of Zhengping; and Chun's nephews Kan and Dun had followed the emperor north of the Yellow River—all came under Hao's suspicion.

sentences.zh: 以椿家世顯重，恐失人望，未及加罪。

translations.literal: Because the Chun family's generations were illustrious and weighty, fearing to lose public esteem, he did not yet impose punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Chun family was too prominent to alienate, Hao did not yet punish them.

sentences.zh: 時人助其憂怖，或有勸椿攜家避禍。

translations.literal: People of the time shared in their fear and dread; some advised Chun to take his family and flee disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Others shared their fear, and some urged Chun to flee with his family to escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「吾內外百口，何處逃竄？

translations.literal: Chun said: "Within and without, a hundred mouths in my household—where could we flee and hide?
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "With a household of a hundred souls, where could we flee?

sentences.zh: 正當坐任運耳。」

translations.literal: One should simply sit and accept fate."
translations.idiomatic: We can only sit and accept whatever comes."

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，椿每辭遜，不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Chun repeatedly declined and yielded; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Chun repeatedly tried to resign, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 上書頻乞歸老，詔曰：「椿國之老成，方所尊尚，遽以高年，願言致仕，顧懷舊德，是以未從。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials repeatedly begging to retire on account of age; an edict said: "Chun is the state's elder of long experience, one whom we honor and esteem; suddenly, at advanced age, he wishes to speak of retirement. Recalling his old merit, we therefore have not followed it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to retire, and an edict replied: "Chun is a pillar of the state whom we honor and esteem; though he now wishes to retire in his old age, we have held back out of regard for his long service.

sentences.zh: 但告謁頻煩，辭理彌固，以茲難奪，又所重違，今便允其雅志。

translations.literal: But his petitions and audiences have been frequent and troublesome, and his reasoning ever firmer; on this account it is hard to override, and again we greatly hesitate to refuse; we now grant his lofty wish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your petitions have been frequent and your resolve firm; though we hesitate to let you go, we now grant your wish.

sentences.zh: 可服侍中朝服，賜服一具、衣一襲、八尺床帳、几杖，不朝，乘安車，駕駟馬，給扶，傳詔二人，仰所在郡縣，時以禮存問安否。

translations.literal: He may attend in Palace Attendant court dress; grant one set of robes, one suit of clothing, an eight-foot bed canopy, a table and staff; he need not attend court; he may ride in a comfort carriage drawn by four horses, with attendants provided; two imperial messengers; charge the commandery and county where he resides to inquire after his well-being from time to time according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He may wear Palace Attendant court dress, and is granted a set of robes, a suit of clothing, an eight-foot bed with canopy, a table, and a staff; he need not attend court but may travel in a comfort carriage drawn by four horses with attendants, accompanied by two imperial messengers; the local commandery and county are charged to inquire after his health according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 方乖詢訪，良用憮然。

translations.literal: Just as we turn from consultation and inquiry, we are deeply saddened.
translations.idiomatic: We are deeply grieved to lose your counsel."

sentences.zh: 」椿奉詔於華林園，帝下御座執椿手流淚曰：「公，先帝舊臣，實為元老，今四方未寧，理須諮訪。

translations.literal: Chun received the edict at Hualin Garden; the emperor descended from the imperial seat, took Chun's hand, and weeping said: "Sir, you are an old minister of the former emperor, truly a senior elder; now the four quarters are not yet at peace, and consultation is rightly required.
translations.idiomatic: Chun received the edict at Hualin Garden. The emperor left his seat, took Chun's hand, and with tears said, "You are a veteran minister of the late emperor and a true elder of the court; with the realm still unsettled, we need your counsel.

sentences.zh: 但高尚其志，決意不留，既難相違，深用悽愴。

translations.literal: But you elevate your ambition and are resolved not to remain; since it is hard to go against you, we are deeply filled with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hold to your lofty resolve and will not stay; though we cannot refuse you, our heart is full of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 」椿亦歔欷，欲拜，莊帝親執不聽。

translations.literal: Chun also sobbed; wishing to bow, Emperor Zhuang personally held him and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chun wept as well; when he tried to bow, Emperor Zhuang held him back and would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 於是賜以絹布，給羽林衞送，羣公百僚餞於城西張方橋，行路觀者，莫不稱歎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted silk and cloth; the Feathered Forest Guard was provided to escort him; the assembled lords and hundred officials saw him off at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city; passersby who watched all praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted silk and cloth and escorted by the Feathered Forest Guard; lords and officials saw him off at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city, and all who watched along the road marveled.

sentences.zh: 椿臨行，誡子孫曰：

translations.literal: As Chun was about to depart, he admonished his descendants, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, Chun admonished his descendants:

sentences.zh: 我家入魏之始，即為上客，給田宅，賜奴婢、馬牛羊，遂成富室。

translations.literal: When our family first entered Wei, we were immediately treated as honored guests; fields and houses were granted, slaves, servants, horses, cattle, and sheep bestowed; we thereby became a wealthy household.
translations.idiomatic: When our family first entered Wei we were treated as honored guests: we were granted fields and houses, given slaves, horses, cattle, and sheep, and soon became a wealthy household.

sentences.zh: 自爾至今二十年，二千石、方伯不絕，祿恤甚多。

translations.literal: From then until now, twenty years—two-thousand-bushel offices and regional lords have been unbroken; salaries and stipends have been very great.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty years since, our family has held one governorship or regional post after another, with generous salaries and stipends.

sentences.zh: 至於親姻知故，吉凶之際，必厚加贈襚；

translations.literal: As for kin by marriage and old acquaintances, at occasions of fortune or misfortune we always added generous gifts and burial offerings;
translations.idiomatic: For relatives and old friends, we have always given generously at weddings, funerals, and other occasions;

sentences.zh: 來往賓僚，必以酒肉飲食。

translations.literal: guests and colleagues who came and went were always provided wine, meat, and food.
translations.idiomatic: and we have always entertained visiting guests and colleagues with food and wine.

sentences.zh: 是故親姻朋友無憾焉。

translations.literal: therefore among kin, marriage connections, and friends there has been no regret.
translations.idiomatic: That is why our kin and friends have had no cause for complaint.

sentences.zh: 國家初，丈夫好服綵色。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, men liked to wear colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the early days of the dynasty, men liked to dress in bright colors.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不記上谷翁時事，然記清河翁時服飾，恒見翁著布衣韋帶，常約敕諸父曰：「汝等後世，脫若富貴於今日者，慎勿積金一斤、綵帛百匹已上，用為富也。

translations.literal: Although I do not remember affairs from Lord Shanggu's time, I remember Lord Qinghe's dress and adornment; I constantly saw the old lord wear plain cloth and a leather belt; he often admonished the elders, saying: "You in later generations—if by chance you become as wealthy as today—take care not to amass more than one jin of gold or more than one hundred bolts of colored silk as your wealth.
translations.idiomatic: I do not remember Lord Shanggu's day, but I remember how Lord Qinghe dressed: he always wore plain cloth and a leather belt, and often warned the elders, "If you later become as wealthy as we are today, do not hoard more than one jin of gold or one hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 」又不聽治生求利，又不聽與勢家作婚姻。

translations.literal: He also did not permit pursuing livelihood for profit, nor did he permit marrying into powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade us to pursue profit in business or to marry into powerful families.

sentences.zh: 至吾兄弟，不能遵奉。

translations.literal: By the time of us brothers, we could not follow and obey.
translations.idiomatic: My brothers and I failed to follow his teaching.

sentences.zh: 今汝等服乘，以漸華好，吾是以知恭儉之德，漸不如上世也。

translations.literal: Now your dress and mounts have gradually become splendid and fine; from this I know that the virtue of respect and frugality has gradually fallen short of the previous generation.
translations.idiomatic: Your dress and mounts have grown finer with each generation, and I can see that the virtue of humility and thrift has declined from our forebears' day.

sentences.zh: 又吾兄弟，若在家，必同盤而食，若有近行，不至，必待其還，亦有過中不食，忍飢相待。

translations.literal: Moreover, we brothers, if at home, always ate from the same dish; if one had a short journey and had not arrived, we always waited for his return; there were also times when we passed midday without eating, enduring hunger while waiting for one another.
translations.idiomatic: When we brothers were at home we always ate from the same dish; if one of us was away on a short trip, the rest waited for his return, sometimes going hungry past midday rather than eat without him.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟八人，今存者有三，是故不忍別食也。

translations.literal: We were eight brothers; now only three remain; therefore we could not bear to eat separately.
translations.idiomatic: We were eight brothers, and only three of us remain; that is why we could not bear to eat apart.

sentences.zh: 又願畢吾兄弟世，不異居、異財，汝等眼見，非為虛假。

translations.literal: Moreover I wished that through our brothers' generation we would not live separately or hold separate property; you have seen this with your own eyes—it is no falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: I also hoped that throughout our generation we would never live apart or divide our property; you have seen this yourselves—it is no empty claim.

sentences.zh: 如聞汝等兄弟，時有別齋獨食者，此又不如吾等一世也。

translations.literal: As I hear, among you brothers there are sometimes those who take separate meals and eat alone; this again falls short of our generation.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that some of you brothers now take separate meals; even in this you fall short of our generation.

sentences.zh: 吾今日不為貧賤，然居住舍宅不作壯麗華飾者，正慮汝等後世不賢，不能保守之，方為勢家作奪。

translations.literal: I am not poor and lowly today, yet I do not make my dwelling and house splendid and ornate because I precisely fear that you in later generations, if unworthy, will be unable to preserve them and they will be seized by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: I am not poor today, yet I keep my house plain because I fear that if later generations prove unworthy they will not be able to hold on to a grand estate and powerful families will seize it.

sentences.zh: 北都時，朝法嚴急。

translations.literal: In the time of the Northern Capital, court law was strict and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was at the Northern Capital, palace discipline was severe.

sentences.zh: 太和初，吾兄弟三人並居內職，兄在高祖左右，吾與津在文明太后左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, we three brothers all held inner court posts; my elder brother was at Emperor Gaozu's side, Jin and I at Empress Dowager Wenming's side.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe all three of us brothers held inner court posts: my elder brother served Emperor Gaozu, while Jin and I served Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 于時口敕，責諸內官，十日仰密得一事，不列便大瞋嫌。

translations.literal: At that time by oral edict the inner officials were charged: within ten days you must secretly obtain one matter; if you do not report it, great anger and displeasure will follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an oral edict charged the inner officials to uncover one secret within ten days; failure to report brought immediate wrath.

sentences.zh: 諸人多有依敕密列者，亦有太后、高祖中間傳言構間者。

translations.literal: Many people secretly reported according to the edict; there were also those who passed words between the empress dowager and Emperor Gaozu and sowed discord.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials secretly informed as ordered, and some carried words between the empress dowager and Emperor Gaozu to sow discord.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟自相誡曰：「今忝二聖近臣，母子間甚難，宜深慎之。

translations.literal: We brothers admonished one another, saying: "Now we disgracefully serve as close ministers to the Two Sovereigns; between mother and son it is very difficult—we ought to be deeply cautious.
translations.idiomatic: We brothers warned one another: "We serve both sovereigns as close ministers; the space between mother and son is perilous, and we must be exceedingly careful.

sentences.zh: 又列人事，亦何容易，縱被瞋責，慎勿輕言。

translations.literal: Moreover, to report people's affairs—how is that easy? Even if we are met with anger and reproach, take care not to speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting on others is no easy matter; even if we are rebuked for silence, we must not speak rashly.

sentences.zh: 」十餘年中，不嘗言一人罪過，當時大被嫌責。

translations.literal: For more than ten years we never spoke of a single person's fault; at the time we were greatly met with displeasure and reproach.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years we never reported anyone's faults, and at the time we were sharply rebuked for it.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「臣等非不聞人言，正恐不審，仰誤聖聽，是以不敢言。

translations.literal: We replied: "We ministers are not that we have not heard people's words; we precisely fear we may not have verified them and would wrongly mislead the sacred hearing—therefore we dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: We answered, "It is not that we hear nothing, but we fear we may not have verified what we hear and would mislead Your Majesties—so we dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 」於後終以不言蒙賞。

translations.literal: Afterward we ultimately received reward for not speaking.
translations.idiomatic: In the end we were rewarded for our silence.

sentences.zh: 及二聖間言語，終不敢輒爾傳通。

translations.literal: As for words between the Two Sovereigns, we ultimately did not dare lightly pass them back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: We never dared casually relay words between the Two Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年，吾從濟州來朝，在清徽堂豫讌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe I came to court from Jizhou and attended a preliminary banquet in Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Taihe I came to court from Jizhou and attended a banquet in Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂諸王、諸貴曰：「北京之日，太后嚴明，吾每得杖，左右因此有是非言語。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to the princes and nobles: "In the days at the Northern Capital, the empress dowager was strict and clear; I was often beaten with the staff; those at my side therefore had right-and-wrong words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said to the princes and nobles, "In the days at the Northern Capital the empress dowager was strict; I was often beaten with the staff, and those around me would speak ill of her.

sentences.zh: 和朕母子者唯楊椿兄弟。

translations.literal: Those who harmonized me, mother and son, were only the brothers Yang Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Only the brothers Yang Chun never set mother and son against each other.

sentences.zh: 」遂舉賜四兄及我酒。

translations.literal: He thereupon raised a cup and granted wine to my four elder brothers and me.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his cup and granted wine to my four elder brothers and me.

sentences.zh: 汝等脫若萬一蒙時主知遇，宜深慎言語，不可輕論人惡也。

translations.literal: You—if by chance you should one day receive the present ruler's recognition and favor—ought to be deeply cautious in speech and must not lightly discuss others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance you should win a ruler's favor, be deeply cautious in speech and never lightly speak ill of others.

sentences.zh: 吾自惟文武才藝、門望姻援不勝他人，一旦位登侍中、尚書，四歷九卿，十為刺史，光祿大夫、儀同、開府、司徒、太保，津今復為司空者，正由忠貞，小心謹慎，口不嘗論人過，無貴無賤，待之以禮，以是故至此耳。

translations.literal: I consider that in civil and military talent, family standing, and marriage connections I do not surpass others; yet in one morning I ascended to Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing, passed through four of the Nine Ministers, served ten times as governor, became Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, received the Three Precedence of Honor, an open office, Duke of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Mentor; Jin is now again Minister of Works—all this is precisely because of loyalty and steadfastness, careful caution, never speaking of others' faults, treating all without regard to noble or base with ritual propriety; for this reason we have reached here.
translations.idiomatic: I know I have never surpassed others in talent, family standing, or marriage connections, yet I rose to Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing, served four times among the Nine Ministers and ten times as governor, and reached Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, the Three Precedence of Honor, an open office, Duke of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Mentor; Jin is now Minister of Works—all because we were loyal, cautious, never spoke of others' faults, and treated everyone, high or low, with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 聞汝等學時俗人，乃有坐而待客者，有驅馳勢門者，有輕論人惡者，及見貴勝則敬重之，見貧賤則慢易之，此人行之大失，立身之大病也。

translations.literal: I hear that you, learning from the customs of the age, have some who sit and wait upon guests, some who rush about to powerful gates, some who lightly discuss others' faults; when they see the noble and eminent they respect and honor them, when they see the poor and base they treat them with contempt—this is a great failure in conduct and a grave disease in establishing oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in imitating worldly ways some of you sit idly waiting on guests, some rush to curry favor with the powerful, and some speak lightly of others' faults; you respect the eminent and despise the poor—such conduct is a grave moral failure.

sentences.zh: 汝家仕皇魏以來，高祖以下乃有七郡太守、三十二州刺史，內外顯職，時流少比。

translations.literal: Since your family entered the service of Imperial Wei, from Emperor Gaozu down there have been seven commandery administrators and thirty-two provincial governors; in inner and outer eminent posts, few of the age can compare.
translations.idiomatic: Since our family entered Wei service, from Emperor Gaozu's day down we have produced seven commandery administrators and thirty-two provincial governors—few families of the age can match our record of high office.

sentences.zh: 汝等若能存禮節，不為奢淫驕慢，假不勝人，足免尤誚，足成名家。

translations.literal: If you can preserve ritual propriety and not be extravagant, dissolute, arrogant, or insolent, even if you do not surpass others, you will suffice to escape blame and reproach and suffice to become a family of renown.
translations.idiomatic: If you preserve propriety and avoid extravagance, debauchery, arrogance, and insolence, even if you never surpass others you will avoid reproach and preserve the family's name.

sentences.zh: 吾今年始七十五，自惟氣力，尚堪朝覲天子，所以孜孜求退者，正欲使汝等知天下滿足之義，為一門法耳，非是苟求千載之名也。

translations.literal: I am only seventy-five this year; considering my strength, I am still able to attend court and behold the Son of Heaven; the reason I diligently seek retirement is precisely to make you know the principle of contentment under heaven and establish a family standard—it is not to grasp after a name for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I am only seventy-five, and still strong enough to attend court; I seek retirement so zealously only to teach you the meaning of contentment and to set a standard for our house—not to chase a name that will last a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 汝等能記吾言，百年之後，終無恨矣。

translations.literal: If you can remember my words, a hundred years hence you will ultimately have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you remember what I say, you will have no regrets a hundred years from now.

sentences.zh: 椿還華陰踰年，普泰元年七月，為尒朱天光所害，年七十七，時人莫不冤痛之。

translations.literal: Chun returned to Huayin for more than a year; in the seventh month of the first year of Putai he was killed by Erzhu Tianguang, aged seventy-seven; people of the time all grieved that it was unjust.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year after returning to Huayin, Chun was killed by Erzhu Tianguang in the seventh month of the first year of Putai, at the age of seventy-seven; all who heard of it grieved at the injustice.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈都督冀定殷相四州諸軍事、太師、丞相、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs of Ji, Ding, Yin, and Xiang and the four provinces, Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored as commander of military affairs in Jizhou, Dingzhou, Yinzhou, and Xiangzhou, Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子昱，字元晷。

translations.literal: His son Yu, styled Yuangui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, styled Yuangui.

sentences.zh: 起家廣平王懷左常侍，懷好武事，數出遊獵，昱每規諫。

translations.literal: He began his career as Left Attendant to Prince Huai of Guangping; Huai loved military affairs and often went out hunting; Yu repeatedly admonished and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Left Attendant to Prince Huai of Guangping; the prince loved military sport and often went hunting, and Yu repeatedly remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 正始中，以京兆、廣平二王國臣，多有縱恣，公行屬請，於是詔御史中尉崔亮窮治之，伏法於都市者三十餘人，其不死者悉除名為民。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, because the retainers of the two princely states of Jingzhao and Guangping were largely unrestrained and openly practiced patronage requests, an edict ordered the Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang to investigate thoroughly; more than thirty were executed in the capital market, and those who were not killed were all stripped of rank and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi many retainers of the Jingzhao and Guangping princely establishments ran wild and openly traded on influence; Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang was ordered to investigate. More than thirty were executed in the capital market, and the rest were struck from the rolls and reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 唯昱與博陵崔楷以忠諫得免。

translations.literal: Only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were spared because of loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were spared because their loyal remonstrance had kept them clear of wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 後除太學博士、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Large.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Large.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書令王肅除揚州刺史，出頓於洛陽東亭，朝貴畢集，詔令諸王送別，昱伯父播同在餞席。

translations.literal: Initially, when Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su was appointed Governor of Yangzhou and went out to halt at Luoyang East Pavilion, the court nobles all assembled; an edict ordered the princes to see him off; Yu's uncle Bo was also at the farewell banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su was appointed Governor of Yangzhou and paused at Luoyang East Pavilion on his way out, the court nobility gathered for his farewell; an edict ordered the princes to see him off, and Yu's uncle Bo was among those at the banquet.

sentences.zh: 酒酣之後，廣陽王嘉、北海王詳等與播論議競理，播不為之屈。

translations.literal: After the wine had warmed them, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others debated principles with Bo in competitive argument; Bo did not yield to them.
translations.idiomatic: After the wine had flowed freely, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others debated Bo in spirited argument, but Bo would not yield.

sentences.zh: 北海顧謂昱曰：「尊伯性剛，不伏理，大不如尊使君也。

translations.literal: Beihai turned and said to Yu: "Your honored uncle is by nature stubborn and will not submit to reason—greatly inferior to your honored father.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang of Beihai turned to Yu and said, "Your uncle is stubborn and will not bow to reason—far inferior to your father.

sentences.zh: 」昱前對曰：「昱父道隆則從其隆，道洿則從其洿；

translations.literal: Yu stepped forward and replied: "Yu's father—if the way is lofty, he follows its loftiness; if the way is muddy, he follows its muddiness;
translations.idiomatic: Yu stepped forward and replied, "My father follows the high road when it is high and the low road when it is low;

sentences.zh: 伯父剛則不吐，柔亦不茹。

translations.literal: My uncle, when hard, will not spit out; when soft, will not swallow.
translations.idiomatic: My uncle, when hard, will not yield; when soft, will not be imposed upon."

sentences.zh: 」一坐歎其能言。

translations.literal: The whole assembly sighed in admiration at his eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly marveled at his wit.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「非此郎，何得申二公之美也。」

translations.literal: Su said: "If not for this young man, how could the virtues of the two gentlemen be expressed?"
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Without this young man, who could have brought out the excellence of those two men?"

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，以本官帶詹事丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanchang, he concurrently held the post of Grand Tutor's Assistant while retaining his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanchang, he was given the additional post of Assistant to the Grand Tutor while keeping his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 于時，肅宗在懷抱之中，至於出入，左右乳母而已，不令宮僚聞知。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Suzong was still in infancy; as for his comings and goings, only the wet nurses at his side knew—palace officials were not permitted to hear of them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Suzong was still an infant in arms. Whenever he went out or came in, only the wet nurses at his side attended him, and the palace staff were kept from knowing.

sentences.zh: 昱諫曰：「陛下不以臣等凡淺，備位宮臣，太子動止，宜令翼從。

translations.literal: Yu remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty did not consider us shallow and mediocre when appointing us as palace officials; the Crown Prince's movements and stops ought to be attended by us as wings and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated, "Your Majesty did not deem us unworthy when you appointed us as palace officials. The Crown Prince's comings and goings ought to be attended by us.

sentences.zh: 然自此以來，輕爾出入，進無二傅輔導之美，退闕羣僚陪侍之式，非所謂示民軌儀，著君臣之義。

translations.literal: Yet since then he has casually come and gone; when going out there lacks the exemplary guidance of the two tutors, when returning there falls short of the established form of the assembled officials attending—this is not what is called showing the people proper conduct and making clear the relationship between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since then he has come and gone with little ceremony. When he goes out, he lacks the tutelage of the two mentors; when he returns, he lacks the formal attendance of the assembled officials. This is not what it means to show the people proper conduct and to make clear the bond between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 陛下若召太子，必降手敕，令臣下咸知，為後世法。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty summons the Crown Prince, you must issue a personal edict so that all officials know, making it a model for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty summons the Crown Prince, you should issue a personal edict so that all your officials know of it and so that posterity may have a model to follow."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔曰：「自今已後，若非朕手敕，勿令兒輒出。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "From now on, unless it is my personal edict, do not let the child go out at will.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "From this day forward, unless I personally command it, the boy is not to go out at will.

sentences.zh: 宮臣在直者，從至萬歲門。」

translations.literal: Palace officials on duty shall accompany him as far as the Gate of Eternal Life."
translations.idiomatic: Palace officials on duty shall accompany him as far as the Gate of Eternal Life."

sentences.zh: 久之，轉太尉掾，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: After some time, he was transferred to Clerk of the Grand Commandant and concurrently served as Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to clerk of the Grand Commandant and concurrently appointed secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘗從容謂昱曰：「今帝年幼，朕親萬機，然自薄德化不能感親姻，在外不稱人心，卿有所聞，慎勿諱隱。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling once spoke to Yu in a relaxed manner: "The Emperor is young now and I personally attend to all affairs; yet my virtue is thin and my influence cannot move my kin—without they do not please people's hearts; if you have heard anything, take care not to conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling once spoke to Yu at her ease: "The Emperor is still young, and I attend to all affairs of state myself. Yet my virtue is slight, and I cannot move my own kin; abroad they do not win people's hearts. If you hear anything, take care not to hide it from me.

sentences.zh: 」昱於是奏揚州刺史李崇五車載貨，恒州刺史楊鈞造銀食器十具，並餉領軍元叉。

translations.literal: Yu then memorialized that Li Chong, Governor of Yangzhou, loaded five carts with goods, and Yang Jun, Governor of Hengzhou, had ten sets of silver dining utensils made, all presenting gifts to the chief commander Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then memorialized that Li Chong, Governor of Yangzhou, had sent five cartloads of goods, and Yang Jun, Governor of Hengzhou, had had ten sets of silver dining vessels made, all as gifts to the chief commander Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 靈太后召叉夫妻泣而責之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Yuan Cha and his wife, weeping as she rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Yuan Cha and his wife and rebuked them through her tears.

sentences.zh: 叉深恨之。

translations.literal: Cha bore a deep grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 昱第六叔舒妻，武昌王和之妹，和即叉之從祖父。

translations.literal: The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the younger sister of Prince of Wuchang He; He was Cha's grand-uncle.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the younger sister of the Prince of Wuchang, He, who was Cha's grand-uncle.

sentences.zh: 舒早喪，有一男六女，及終喪而元氏頻請別居。

translations.literal: Shu died early, leaving one son and six daughters; when the mourning period ended the Yuan family repeatedly asked to live separately.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had died young, leaving one son and six daughters. When the mourning period ended, the Yuan family repeatedly asked to set up a separate household.

sentences.zh: 昱父椿乃集親姻泣而謂曰：「我弟不幸早終，今男未婚，女未嫁，何怱怱便求離居？

translations.literal: Yu's father Chun gathered the kin and weeping said: "My younger brother unfortunately died early; now his son is not yet married and his daughters not yet given in marriage—why so hastily ask to live apart?
translations.idiomatic: Yu's father Chun gathered the kinfolk and, weeping, said, "My younger brother died untimely. His son is not yet married and his daughters not yet betrothed—why this haste to live apart?

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: They would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂懷憾焉。

translations.literal: Thus they harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: From this they nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年，瀛州民劉宣明謀反，事覺逃竄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengui, Liu Xuanming of Yingzhou plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered he fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengui, Liu Xuanming, a commoner of Yingzhou, plotted rebellion. When the plot was discovered, he fled.

sentences.zh: 叉乃使和及元氏誣告昱藏隱宣明，云：「父定州刺史椿、叔華州刺史津，並送甲仗三百具，謀圖不逞。

translations.literal: Cha then had He and the Yuan family lodge a false accusation that Yu was hiding Xuanming, saying: "His father Chun, Governor of Dingzhou, and his uncle Jin, Governor of Huazhou, each sent three hundred sets of armor and weapons, plotting rebellion unsuccessfully.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then had He and the Yuan family lodge a false accusation that Yu was harboring Xuanming, saying, "His father Chun, Governor of Dingzhou, and his uncle Jin, Governor of Huazhou, each sent three hundred sets of armor and weapons in a failed plot of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」叉又構成其事。

translations.literal: Cha also fabricated the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: Cha also fabricated the entire affair.

sentences.zh: 乃遣左右御仗五百人，夜圍昱宅而收之，並無所獲。

translations.literal: He then dispatched five hundred bodyguards from his personal guard, who by night surrounded Yu's residence to arrest him, yet found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent five hundred of his personal guards, who by night surrounded Yu's house to arrest him, but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 靈太后問其狀，昱具對元氏遘釁之端，言至哀切。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling questioned the circumstances; Yu fully answered regarding the Yuan family's provocative origins, speaking with utmost grief and earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling questioned the circumstances. Yu answered in full regarding how the Yuan family had provoked the trouble, speaking with the utmost grief and earnestness.

sentences.zh: 太后乃解昱縛，和及元氏並處死刑，而叉相左右，和直免官，元氏卒亦不坐。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then released Yu from his bonds; He and the Yuan family were both sentenced to death, but with Cha's influence on both sides, He was merely stripped of office and the Yuan family in the end was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then released Yu from his bonds. He and the Yuan family were both sentenced to death, but with Cha's influence on either side, He was merely dismissed from office and the Yuan family in the end went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 及元叉之廢，太后乃出昱為濟陰內史。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha was deposed, the Empress Dowager sent Yu out to serve as Internal Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha was deposed, the Empress Dowager sent Yu out to serve as Internal Administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 中山王熙起兵於鄴，叉遣黃門盧同詣鄴刑熙，并窮黨與。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Xi raised troops at Ye; Cha sent Palace Attendant Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and exhaustively pursue his accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan, Xi, raised troops at Ye. Cha sent Palace Attendant Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and to pursue his accomplices to the end.

sentences.zh: 同希叉旨，就郡鎖昱赴鄴，訊百日，後乃還任。

translations.literal: Tong, hoping to please Cha's intent, had Yu seized in the commandery and taken to Ye; after a hundred days of interrogation he was finally returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, eager to please Cha, had Yu seized in the commandery and taken to Ye. After a hundred days of interrogation, Yu was at last returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除征虜將軍、中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Secretariat Gentleman, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Secretariat Gentleman, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時北鎮饑民二十餘萬，詔昱為使，分散於冀、定、瀛三州就食。

translations.literal: At that time more than two hundred thousand hungry people from the northern garrisons—an edict appointed Yu as envoy to disperse them across the three commanderies of Ji, Ding, and Ying to obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than two hundred thousand starving people from the northern garrisons needed relief. An edict appointed Yu as envoy to disperse them across Ji, Ding, and Ying to find food.

sentences.zh: 後賊圍豳州，詔昱兼侍中，持節催西北道大都督、北海王顥，仍隨軍監察。

translations.literal: Later when bandits besieged Binzhou, Yu was appointed concurrent Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to urge the Grand Commander of the Northwest Route, Prince of Beihai Hao, and continued with the army as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when bandits besieged Binzhou, Yu was appointed concurrent Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to urge on the Grand Commander of the Northwest Route, the Prince of Beihai, Hao, and he continued with the army as inspector.

sentences.zh: 豳州圍解。

translations.literal: The siege of Binzhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Binzhou was lifted.

sentences.zh: 雍州蜀賊張映龍、姜神達知州內空虛，謀欲攻掩，刺史元脩義懼而請援，一日一夜，書移九通。

translations.literal: In Yongzhou, the Shu bandits Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda, knowing the province was empty within, plotted a surprise attack; Governor Yuan Xiuyi in fear requested relief—in one day and one night he sent nine dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzhou, the Shu bandits Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda, knowing the province was hollowed out within, plotted a surprise attack. Governor Yuan Xiuyi, in fear, requested relief, sending nine dispatches in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 都督李叔仁遲疑不赴。

translations.literal: The Area Commander Li Shuren hesitated and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: The area commander Li Shuren hesitated and would not go.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「長安，關中基本。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Chang'an is the foundation of the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Chang'an is the foundation of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 今大軍頓在涇豳，與賊相對，若使長安不守，大軍自然瓦散，此軍雖往，有何益也！

translations.literal: Now the main army is halted at Jing and Bin, facing the bandits; if Chang'an is not held, the main army will naturally crumble like tiles—what use would this force be even if it went!
translations.idiomatic: The main army is now halted at Jing and Bin, facing the bandits. If Chang'an is not held, the main army will collapse of its own accord. What good would it do for this force to go?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與叔仁等俱進，於陳斬神達及諸賊四百許人，餘悉奔散。

translations.literal: Then he advanced together with Shuren and the others; in battle he beheaded Shenda and some four hundred bandits, and the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced together with Shuren and the others. In battle they beheaded Shenda and some four hundred bandits, and the rest all fled.

sentences.zh: 詔以昱受旨催督，而顥軍稽緩，遂免昱官。

translations.literal: An edict held that Yu had received orders to urge and supervise, yet Hao's army had been slow, and so Yu was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict held that although Yu had received orders to urge the army on, Hao's forces had been slow, and so Yu was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 乃兼侍中催軍。

translations.literal: He was then concurrently appointed Palace Attendant to urge on the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant to urge on the army.

sentences.zh: 尋除征虜將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，昱父椿出為雍州刺史，徵昱還，除吏部郎中、武衞將軍，轉北中郎將，加安東將軍。

translations.literal: Before long, Yu's father Chun went out as Governor of Yongzhou; Yu was summoned back and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel, General of the Martial Guard, then transferred to General of the North, with added title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu's father Chun went out as Governor of Yongzhou. Yu was recalled and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and General of the Martial Guard, then transferred to General of the North with the added title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤等敗於關中，以昱兼七兵尚書、持節、假撫軍將軍、都督，防守雍州。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was given concurrent appointment as Minister of the Seven Arms, bearing the staff, acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and Area Commander to defend Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was appointed concurrent Minister of the Seven Arms, bearing the staff, acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and area commander to defend Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 昱遇賊失利而返。

translations.literal: Yu encountered the bandits, suffered defeat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu met the bandits, suffered defeat, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 除度支尚書，轉撫軍、徐州刺史，尋除鎮東將軍、假車騎將軍、東南道都督，又加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Revenue, transferred as Pacifying Army [general] and Governor of Xuzhou; soon appointed General Who Guards the East, acting General of Cavalry and Chariots, Commander of the Southeast Route, with added title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Revenue, then transferred to Pacifying Army general and Governor of Xuzhou. Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East, acting General of Cavalry and Chariots, and commander of the Southeast Route, with the added title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後太山太守羊侃據郡南叛，蕭衍遣將軍王辯率眾侵寇徐州，番郡人續靈珍受衍平北將軍、番郡刺史，[6]擁眾一萬，攻逼番城。

translations.literal: Later Taishan Administrator Yang Kan held the commandery and rebelled to the south; Xiao Yan sent General Wang Bian leading troops to invade and raid Xuzhou; Xu Lingzhen of Fanyang, having received from Yan the titles of General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Fanyang, with ten thousand men pressed the attack on Fanyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taishan Administrator Yang Kan held the commandery and rebelled southward. Xiao Yan sent General Wang Bian at the head of an army to invade Xuzhou. Xu Lingzhen of Fanyang, having received from Yan the titles of General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Fanyang, led ten thousand men in an assault on Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 昱遣別將劉馘擊破之，臨陳斬靈珍首，王辯退走。

translations.literal: Yu sent detached commander Liu Huo to defeat them; in battle he beheaded Lingzhen, and Wang Bian retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent detached commander Liu Huo to defeat them. In battle Lingzhen was beheaded, and Wang Bian retreated.

sentences.zh: 侃兄深，時為徐州行臺，府州咸欲禁深。

translations.literal: Kan's elder brother Shen, who was then Xuzhou Mobile Office chief—both the office and the province wanted to detain Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's elder brother Shen was then chief of the Xuzhou mobile office, and both the office and the province wanted to detain him.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「昔叔向不以鮒也見廢，春秋貴之，奈何以侃罪深也。

translations.literal: Yu said: "In antiquity Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of his fish-cook son; the Spring and Autumn Annals praised this—how can we punish Shen for Kan's crime?
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "In antiquity Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of his son, the fish-cook. The Spring and Autumn Annals praised this. How can we punish Shen for Kan's crime?

sentences.zh: 宜聽朝旨。

translations.literal: We ought to await the court's decision.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to await the court's decision."

sentences.zh: 」不許羣議。

translations.literal: He did not permit the assembly's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He would not allow the assembly's proposal.

sentences.zh: 還朝。

translations.literal: He returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，屬元顥侵逼大梁，除昱征東將軍、右光祿大夫，加散騎常侍、使持節、假車騎將軍，為南道大都督，鎮滎陽。

translations.literal: Before long, as Yuan Hao pressed upon Daliang, Yu was appointed General Who Campaigns East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right, with added titles of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, acting General of Cavalry and Chariots, Grand Commander of the South Route, stationed at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as Yuan Hao pressed upon Daliang, Yu was appointed General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right, with the added titles of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, and acting General of Cavalry and Chariots, and was made Grand Commander of the South Route, stationed at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 顥既擒濟陰王暉業，乘虛徑進，大兵集於城下，遣其左衞劉業、王道安等招昱，令降，昱不從，顥遂攻之。

translations.literal: Hao having captured Prince of Jiyin Huiye, seized the opportunity to advance directly; his great army gathered below the walls; he sent his Left Guard Liu Ye, Wang Dao'an and others to summon Yu to surrender—Yu refused, and Hao then attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, having captured the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, seized the opportunity to advance directly. His great army gathered below the walls. He sent his Left Guard Liu Ye, Wang Dao'an, and others to summon Yu to surrender. Yu refused, and Hao then attacked.

sentences.zh: 城陷，都督元恭，太守、西河王悰並踰城而走，俱被擒縶。

translations.literal: The city fell; Area Commander Yuan Gong, Administrator and Prince of Xihe Cong both fled over the walls and were all captured and bound.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. Area Commander Yuan Gong, and the Administrator and Prince of Xihe, Cong, both fled over the walls and were all captured and bound.

sentences.zh: 昱與弟息五人，在門樓上，須臾顥至，執昱下城，面責昱曰：「楊昱，卿今死甘心否？

translations.literal: Yu with five younger brothers and sons was on the gate tower; presently Hao arrived, seized Yu and brought him down from the wall; facing him he rebuked Yu: "Yang Yu, are you now content to die?
translations.idiomatic: Yu, with five younger brothers and sons, was on the gate tower. Presently Hao arrived, seized Yu, and brought him down from the wall. Facing him, he rebuked Yu: "Yang Yu, are you now content to die?

sentences.zh: 卿自負我，非我負卿也。

translations.literal: You betrayed me—I did not betray you.
translations.idiomatic: You betrayed me. I did not betray you."

sentences.zh: 」昱答曰：「分不望生，向所以不下樓者，正慮亂兵耳。

translations.literal: Yu replied: "By my lot I do not hope to live; the reason I did not come down earlier was precisely because I feared the disorderly soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "By my lot I do not hope to live. The reason I did not come down earlier was precisely that I feared the disorderly soldiers.

sentences.zh: 但恨八十老父，無人供養，負病黃泉，求乞小弟一命，便死不朽也。

translations.literal: Only I regret my eighty-year-old father with no one to support him, going to the yellow springs burdened with illness—I beg you to spare one younger brother's life, and then my death would be imperishable.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that my eighty-year-old father has no one to support him and must go to the yellow springs burdened with illness. I beg you to spare one younger brother's life, and then my death would not be in vain."

sentences.zh: 」顥乃拘之。

translations.literal: Hao then detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then detained him.

sentences.zh: 明旦，顥將陳慶之、胡光等三百餘人伏顥帳前，請曰：「陛下渡江三千里，無遺鏃之費，昨日一朝殺傷五百餘人，求乞楊昱以快意。

translations.literal: The next morning, Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang and more than three hundred others prostrated themselves before Hao's tent and requested: "Your Majesty crossed the river three thousand li without losing a single arrow; yesterday in one morning more than five hundred were killed and wounded—we beg Yang Yu to satisfy our wrath.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang, and more than three hundred others prostrated themselves before Hao's tent and requested, "Your Majesty crossed the river three thousand li without losing a single arrow. Yesterday, in one morning, more than five hundred were killed and wounded. We beg Yang Yu to satisfy our wrath.

sentences.zh: 」顥曰：「我在江東，嘗聞梁主言，初下都日，袁昂為吳郡不降，稱其忠節。

translations.literal: Hao said: "When I was east of the Yangtze I once heard Emperor Liang speak: on the day he first descended on the capital, Yuan Ang as Administrator of Wu commandery did not surrender, and he praised his loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "When I was east of the Yangtze I once heard the Liang emperor say that on the day he first descended on the capital, Yuan Ang, as Administrator of Wu commandery, did not surrender, and he praised his loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 奈何殺楊昱？

translations.literal: How can we kill Yang Yu?
translations.idiomatic: How then can we kill Yang Yu?

sentences.zh: 自此之外，任卿等所請。

translations.literal: Beyond this, I leave you free to request what you wish.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, I leave you free to ask what you will."

sentences.zh: 」於是斬昱下統帥三十七人，皆令蜀兵刳腹取心食之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beheaded Yu along with thirty-seven subordinate commanders below him; all were made to have their bellies cut open and hearts extracted by Shu soldiers to be eaten.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he beheaded Yu along with thirty-seven subordinate commanders beneath him. Shu soldiers cut open their bellies, took out their hearts, and ate them.

sentences.zh: 顥既入洛，除昱名為民。

translations.literal: After Hao entered Luoyang, he struck Yu's name from the rolls and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao entered Luoyang, he struck Yu's name from the rolls and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 孝莊還宮，還復前官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Yu was restored to his former offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Yu was restored to his former offices.

sentences.zh: 及父椿辭老，請解官從養，詔不許。

translations.literal: When his father Chun asked leave on grounds of old age, Yu requested to resign office to care for him—the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Chun asked leave on grounds of old age, Yu requested to resign his office to care for him, but the edict did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，昱為東道行臺，率眾拒尒朱仲遠。

translations.literal: At Erzhu Rong's death, Yu served as Mobile Office chief of the East Route and led troops to resist Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Erzhu Rong's death, Yu served as chief of the East Route mobile office and led troops to resist Erzhu Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 會尒朱兆入洛，昱還京師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yu returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yu returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，亦為天光所害。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district and was also killed by Tian Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to his home district and was also killed by Tian Guang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈都督瀛定二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空公、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded command over all military affairs of the two provinces of Ying and Ding, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Duke of Sikong, and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously awarded command over all military affairs of Ying and Ding, the title Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Duke of Sikong, and the governorship of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子孝邕，員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyong was an External Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoyong served as an external clerk.

sentences.zh: 走免，匿於蠻中，潛結渠帥，謀應齊獻武王以誅尒朱氏。

translations.literal: He escaped, hid among the barbarians, secretly allied with tribal chiefs, and plotted to respond to Qi Xianwu Wang to execute the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped, hid among the barbarians, secretly allied with tribal chiefs, and plotted to respond to Qi Xianwu Wang in exterminating the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 微服入洛，參伺機會。

translations.literal: Disguised in common clothes he entered Luoyang to watch for an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Disguised in common clothes, he entered Luoyang to watch for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 為人所告，世隆收付廷尉，掠殺之。

translations.literal: He was reported by someone; Shilong had him arrested and delivered to the Court of Justice, where he was tortured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported him. Shilong had him arrested and delivered to the Court of Justice, where he was tortured to death.

sentences.zh: 椿弟穎，字惠哲。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Ying, styled Huizhe.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Ying, whose style name was Huizhe.

sentences.zh: 本州別駕。

translations.literal: Provincial Attendant of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial attendant of his native province.

sentences.zh: 子叔良，武定中，新安太守。

translations.literal: His son Shuliang, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuliang, in the Wuding era, served as Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 穎弟順，字延和，寬裕謹厚。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Shun, styled Yanhe, was generous, temperate, and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Shun, whose style name was Yanhe, was generous, temperate, and earnest.

sentences.zh: 太和中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, he first entered service as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he first entered service as a court gentleman for imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 累遷直閤將軍、北中郎將、兼武衞將軍、太僕卿。

translations.literal: He rose through successive appointments to General of the Direct Gate, General of the North, concurrent General of the Martial Guard, and Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to General of the Direct Gate, General of the North, concurrent General of the Martial Guard, and Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 預立莊帝之功，封三門縣開國公，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Having participated in the achievement of establishing Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Sanmen with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken part in the achievement of establishing Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Sanmen with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出為平北將軍、冀州刺史，尋進號撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jizhou; soon his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jizhou, and soon his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 罷州還，遇害，年六十五。

translations.literal: Returning after leaving his governorship, he met with violent death at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his governorship and returning home, he met with violent death at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈都督相殷二州諸軍事、太尉公、錄尚書事、相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded command over all military affairs of the two provinces of Xiang and Yin, Duke of Grand Commandant, Manager of Affairs for the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously awarded command over all military affairs of Xiang and Yin, the title Duke of Grand Commandant, the post of Manager of Affairs for the Imperial Secretariat, and the governorship of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子辯，字僧達。

translations.literal: His son Bian, styled Sengda.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bian, whose style name was Sengda.

sentences.zh: 歷通直常侍、平東將軍、東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as regular attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辯弟仲宣，有風度才學。

translations.literal: Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had bearing, talent, and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had bearing, talent, and learning.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請稍遷太尉掾、中書舍人、通直散騎侍郎、加鎮遠將軍，賜爵弘農男。

translations.literal: Starting as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience he gradually rose to Clerk of the Grand Commandant, Secretary of the Secretariat, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, with added title General Who Calms the Distance, and was granted the enfeoffment of Baron of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a court gentleman for imperial audience, he gradually rose to clerk of the Grand Commandant, secretary in the Secretariat, and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, with the added title General Who Calms the Distance, and was granted the enfeoffment of Baron of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 建義初，遷通直常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he was transferred to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was transferred to regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為平西將軍、正平太守，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Administrator of Zhengping, and his enfeoffment was advanced to Count.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Administrator of Zhengping, and his enfeoffment was advanced to count.

sentences.zh: 在郡有能名，就加安西將軍。

translations.literal: While in the commandery he gained a reputation for competence, and on the spot was given the added title General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: While in the commandery he gained a reputation for competence, and on the spot was given the added title General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 還京之日，兄弟與父同遇害。

translations.literal: On the day he returned to the capital, he and his brothers together with their father met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he returned to the capital, he and his brothers met violent death together with their father.

sentences.zh: 辯，太昌初贈使持節、都督燕恒二州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、恒州刺史；

translations.literal: Bian, at the beginning of Taichang, was posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, command over all military affairs of the two provinces of Yan and Heng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Merit Equal to Three Offices, and Governor of Hengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Bian, at the beginning of Taichang, was posthumously awarded bearer of the staff with full powers, command over all military affairs of Yan and Heng, the title General of Chariots and Cavalry, merit equal to three offices, and the governorship of Hengzhou;

sentences.zh: 仲宣，贈都督青光二州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、尚書右僕射、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan was posthumously awarded command over all military affairs of the two provinces of Qing and Guang, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan was posthumously awarded command over all military affairs of Qing and Guang, the title General of Chariots and Cavalry, the post of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and the governorship of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲宣子玄就，幼而俊拔。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu was brilliant and precocious from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu was brilliant and precocious from childhood.

sentences.zh: 收捕時年九歲，牽挽兵人，謂曰：「欲害諸尊，乞先就死。

translations.literal: At the time of arrest he was nine years old; he tugged at the soldiers and said: "If you wish to harm my elders, I beg to die first.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the arrest he was nine years old. He tugged at the soldiers and said, "If you wish to harm my elders, I beg to die first.

sentences.zh: 」兵人以刀斫斷其臂，猶請死不止，遂先殺之。

translations.literal: The soldiers with their blades cut off his arm; he still unceasingly begged to die, and so they killed him first.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cut off his arm with their blades, yet he still unceasingly begged to die, and so they killed him first.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，贈汝陰太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he was posthumously awarded as Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi he was posthumously awarded the title Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 仲宣弟測，朱衣直閤。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's younger brother Ce was a Direct Gate Attendant in Red Robes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's younger brother Ce served as a direct gate attendant in red robes.

sentences.zh: 亦同時見害。

translations.literal: He too was killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，贈都督平營二州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、吏部尚書、平州刺史。

translations.literal: During Taichang, he was posthumously granted command over all military affairs of Ping and Ying provinces, the title General Who Guards the North, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as commander of military affairs for Ping and Ying provinces, General Who Guards the North, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 測弟稚卿，太昌中，為尚書右丞，坐事死。

translations.literal: Ce's younger brother Zhijing, during Taichang, served as Right Director of the Masters of Writing and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's younger brother Zhijing served as Right Director of the Masters of Writing during Taichang and was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 順弟津，字羅漢，本名延祚，高祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Jin, styled Luohan, originally named Yanzuo, was given his name by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Jin, whose style name was Luohan, had originally been named Yanzuo; Emperor Xiaowen gave him his present name.

sentences.zh: 少端謹，以器度見稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was upright and careful, and was praised for his bearing and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was upright and careful, and won renown for his bearing and magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 年十一，除侍御中散。

translations.literal: At age eleven he was appointed Attendant Cavalier-at-Arms.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of eleven he was appointed an attendant cavalier-at-arms.

sentences.zh: 于時高祖沖幼，文明太后臨朝，津曾久侍左右，忽咳逆失聲，遂吐數升，藏衣袖。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu was still young and Empress Dowager Wenming held court; Jin had long attended at her side when he suddenly coughed violently and lost his voice, then vomited several sheng and hid it in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was still a child and Empress Dowager Wenming held the regency. Jin had long served at her side when he suddenly coughed violently, lost his voice, and vomited several pints of blood, which he concealed in his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 太后聞聲，閱而不見，問其故，具以實言。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager heard the sound, looked about but did not see it, asked the reason, and he told her the whole truth.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager heard the sound, looked around but saw nothing, asked what had happened, and he told her the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 遂以敬慎見知，賜縑百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became known for reverence and caution, and was given one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby won recognition for his reverence and discretion, and was awarded one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷符璽郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Seals within the Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to master of seals within the Department.

sentences.zh: 津以身在禁密，不外交遊，至於宗族姻表，罕相祗候。

translations.literal: Because Jin held a post in the inner and secret service, he did not associate abroad, and even toward kinsmen and affinal relatives he rarely paid calls of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jin served in the inner and confidential offices, he did not socialize outside court, and even toward kinsmen and in-laws he rarely paid courtesy calls.

sentences.zh: 司徒馮誕與津少結交遊，而津見其貴寵，每恒退避，及相招命，多辭疾不往。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Feng Dan and Jin had been friends since youth, but Jin, seeing Dan's noble favor, always kept his distance; when summoned, he often pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Feng Dan and Jin had been friends since youth, but Jin, seeing Dan's lofty favor at court, always kept his distance, and when summoned he often pleaded illness and declined to come.

sentences.zh: 誕以為恨，而津逾遠焉。

translations.literal: Dan resented this, while Jin kept himself even farther away.
translations.idiomatic: Dan took this as a grievance, while Jin kept himself even farther away.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之曰：「司徒，君之少舊，宜蒙進達，何遽自外也？

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "The Minister of Works is an old friend of yours from youth; you ought to receive advancement through him—why so suddenly keep yourself apart?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "The Minister of Works is an old friend of yours from youth; you ought to benefit from his patronage—why so suddenly keep yourself apart?"

sentences.zh: 」津曰：「為勢家所厚，復何容易。

translations.literal: Jin said, "To be favored by a powerful house—how could that be easy afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin replied, "To be favored by a powerful house is no easy thing to live with afterward."

sentences.zh: 但全吾今日，亦以足矣。」

translations.literal: But to preserve myself as I am today is already enough."
translations.idiomatic: But to preserve myself as I am today is already enough."

sentences.zh: 出除征虜將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Campaigns Against Bandits and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out and appointed General Who Campaigns Against Bandits and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 津巨細躬親，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Jin personally attended to matters great and small without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin personally attended to every detail of governance and never slackened.

sentences.zh: 有武功民，齎絹三匹，去城十里，為賊所劫。

translations.literal: A man of Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk; ten li from the city he was robbed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk when, ten li from the city, he was robbed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 時有使者馳驛而至，被劫人因以告之。

translations.literal: At that time an envoy arrived by post-horse, and the robbed man therefore told him.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial courier happened to arrive by post-horse just then, and the robbed man told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 使者到州，以狀白津。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached the province he reported the matter to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the courier reached the province he reported the matter to Jin.

sentences.zh: 津乃下教云：「有人著某色衣，乘某色馬，在城東十里被殺，[7]不知姓名，若有家人，可速收視。

translations.literal: Jin then issued an order saying, "Someone wearing such-and-such colored clothes and riding such-and-such colored horse was killed ten li east of the city,[7] his name unknown; if he has family, let them come quickly to claim the body."
translations.idiomatic: Jin then issued a proclamation: "A man wearing such-and-such colored clothes and riding such-and-such colored horse was killed ten li east of the city,[7] his name unknown; if he has kin, let them come at once to claim the body."

sentences.zh: 」有一老母，行出而哭，云是己子。

translations.literal: An old woman came out weeping as she walked, saying he was her son.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman came out weeping, saying the victim was her son.

sentences.zh: 於是遣騎追收，并絹俱獲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent horsemen in pursuit and recovered both the man and the silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent horsemen in pursuit and recovered both the man and the silk.

sentences.zh: 自是闔境畏服。

translations.literal: From then on the whole jurisdiction feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the whole jurisdiction stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 至於守令僚佐有瀆貨者，未曾公言其罪，常以私書切責之。

translations.literal: As for prefects, magistrates, and staff who took bribes, he never publicly declared their crimes but always rebuked them sharply in private letters.
translations.idiomatic: When prefects, magistrates, or staff took bribes, he never announced their crimes in public but always rebuked them sharply in private letters.

sentences.zh: 於是官屬感厲，莫有犯法。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials were moved and inspired, and none violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: The officials were so moved that none dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，起為右將軍、華州刺史，與兄播前後皆牧本州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Late in Yanzhang he was recalled as General of the Right and Governor of Huazhou; he and his elder brother Bo both in succession governed their native province, and their contemporaries honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yanzhang he was recalled as General of the Right and Governor of Huazhou. He and his elder brother Bo had both in turn governed their native province, and their contemporaries regarded this as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 先是，受調絹匹，度尺特長，在事因緣，共相進退，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Previously, in collecting tax silk, the measuring rod was made especially long; officials took advantage of one another and colluded, and the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when tax silk was collected the measuring rod had been made deliberately long; officials colluded with one another over it, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 津乃令依公尺度其輸物，尤好者賜以杯酒而出；

translations.literal: Jin then ordered that deliveries be measured by the standard rod; those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then ordered that all deliveries be measured by the standard rod. Those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine before dismissing the bearer.

sentences.zh: 所輸少劣，亦為受之，但無酒，以示其耻。

translations.literal: Even inferior deliveries he accepted, but without wine, to show their shame.
translations.idiomatic: Even inferior deliveries he accepted, but without the wine, to mark their shame.

sentences.zh: 於是人競相勸，官調更勝舊日。

translations.literal: Thereupon people competed to encourage one another, and official collections surpassed those of former days.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon people vied to improve their deliveries, and official collections surpassed those of earlier times.

sentences.zh: 還除北中郎將，帶河內太守。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed General of the Northern Central Command and concurrently Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed General of the Northern Central Command with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 太后疑津貳己，不欲使其處河山之要，轉平北將軍、肆州刺史，仍轉并州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager suspected Jin of divided loyalty toward her and did not wish him to hold a key position between the Yellow River and the mountains; he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sizhou, then transferred again to Governor of Bingzhou, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager suspected Jin of disloyalty to her and did not want him holding a strategic post between the Yellow River and the Taihang Mountains. He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sizhou, then moved again to Governor of Bingzhou, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 徵拜右衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，加散騎常侍，尋以本官行定州事。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaochang he was given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and soon with his existing rank acted as governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang he was given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and soon assumed charge of Dingzhou affairs in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 既而近鎮擾亂，侵逼舊京，乃加津安北將軍、假撫軍將軍、北道大都督、右衞，尋轉左衞，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward nearby garrisons were in turmoil and pressed upon the old capital; Jin was then given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the North, Acting General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Commander of the Northern Route, and Right Guard; soon he was transferred to Left Guard and given the title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward nearby garrisons fell into turmoil and threatened the old capital. Jin was then given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the North, Acting General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Commander of the Northern Route, and Right Guard; soon he was transferred to Left Guard and promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 始津受命，出據靈丘，而賊帥鮮于脩禮起於博陵，定州危急，遂回師南赴。

translations.literal: When Jin first received his commission he went out and held Lingqiu, but the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling; Dingzhou was in peril, and he therefore turned his army south.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin first received his commission he marched out and took position at Lingqiu, but the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling and Dingzhou was in grave peril, so he turned his army south.

sentences.zh: 始至城下，營壘未立，而州軍新敗。

translations.literal: He had just reached the foot of the city when his camp was not yet established and the provincial army had newly been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just reached the city when his camp was not yet established and the provincial army had suffered a fresh defeat.

sentences.zh: 津以賊既乘勝，士眾勞疲，柵壘未安，不可擬敵，賊必夜至，則萬無一全，欲移軍入城，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Jin reasoned that the bandits, having seized victory, would find his troops weary and his palisades unsettled and thus no match for the enemy; if the bandits came by night there would be no chance of survival, and he wished to move his army into the city and plan another effort later.
translations.idiomatic: Jin judged that the bandits, riding their victory, would find his troops exhausted and his defenses unfinished and therefore impossible to match; if the bandits came by night not one man would survive. He wanted to move his army into the city and plan another effort later.

sentences.zh: 刺史元固稱賊既逼城，不可示弱，閉門不內。

translations.literal: Governor Yuan Gu said that since the bandits were already pressing the city, one must not show weakness, and closed the gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuan Gu argued that with the bandits already at the walls the city must not show weakness; he shut the gates and refused to admit them.

sentences.zh: 津揮刀欲斬門者，軍乃得入城。

translations.literal: Jin swung his blade intending to cut down the gatekeepers, and only then did the army enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jin drew his sword to strike down the gatekeepers, and only then was his army admitted into the city.

sentences.zh: 賊果夜至，見柵空而去。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came by night, saw the empty palisades, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did come by night, found the camp deserted, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後，賊攻州城東面，已入羅城，刺史閉小城東門，城中慅擾，不敢出戰。

translations.literal: Afterward the bandits attacked the eastern side of the provincial city and had already entered the outer wall; the governor closed the small eastern gate of the inner city, and within the city there was panic and no one dared go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandits attacked the eastern side of the provincial city and broke into the outer wall. The governor shut the small eastern gate of the inner city; panic spread through the city and no one dared go out to fight.

sentences.zh: 津欲禦賊，長史許被守門不聽，津手劍擊被，不中，被乃走。

translations.literal: Jin wished to meet the bandits, but Chief Clerk Xu Bei guarded the gate and would not allow it; Jin struck at Bei with his sword, missed, and Bei then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jin wanted to meet the bandits in battle, but Chief Clerk Xu Bei guarded the gate and refused to allow it. Jin struck at Bei with his sword, missed, and Bei fled.

sentences.zh: 津開門出戰，斬賊帥一人，殺賊數百。

translations.literal: Jin opened the gate and went out to battle, beheading one bandit chief and killing several hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jin opened the gate and went out to fight, beheading one bandit chief and killing several hundred bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊退，人心少安。

translations.literal: The bandits withdrew, and the people's hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits withdrew, and morale in the city steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 詔除衞尉卿，征官如故，以津兄衞尉卿椿代為左衞。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Minister of the Guard, his field rank unchanged; Jin's elder brother Chun, Minister of the Guard, was made Left Guard in his place.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Minister of the Guard while retaining his field command; Jin's elder brother Chun, also Minister of the Guard, was made General of the Left Guard in his stead.

sentences.zh: 尋加鎮軍將軍、討虜都督，兼吏部尚書、北道行臺。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Commander Who Campaigns Against Bandits, with concurrent appointment as Director of the Masters of Writing and Northern Route Executive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Commander Who Campaigns Against Bandits, with concurrent appointment as Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Northern Route Executive.

sentences.zh: 初，津兄椿得罪此州，由鉅鹿人趙略投書所致。
