translations.literal: Earlier Jin's elder brother Chun had fallen afoul of this province because Zhao Lue of Julu had sent in a letter denouncing him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jin's elder brother Chun had gotten into trouble in this province because Zhao Lue of Julu had sent in a denunciatory letter.

sentences.zh: 及津之至，略舉家逃走，津乃下教慰喻，令其還業。

translations.literal: When Jin arrived, Lue fled with his whole household; Jin then issued an order of reassurance and told him to return to his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin arrived, Lue fled with his entire family. Jin issued a reassuring proclamation and told him to return to his livelihood.

sentences.zh: 於是闔州愧服，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole province submitted in shame, and near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The whole province submitted in shame, and people near and far praised him.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥薛脩禮、[8]杜洛周殘掠州境。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chiefs Xue Xiuli[8] and Du Luozhou ravaged the borders of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit chiefs Xue Xiuli[8] and Du Luozhou were ravaging the province.

sentences.zh: 孤城獨立，在兩寇之間，津貯積柴粟，脩理戰具，更營雉堞，賊每來攻，機械競起。

translations.literal: The isolated city stood alone between two enemies; Jin stored firewood and grain, repaired weapons, rebuilt the battlements, and whenever the bandits came to attack, engines of war sprang up everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood alone between two enemy forces. Jin stockpiled firewood and grain, repaired weapons, rebuilt the battlements, and whenever the bandits attacked, engines of war sprang up on every side.

sentences.zh: 又於城中去城十步，掘地至泉，廣作地道，潛兵涌出，置爐鑄鐵，持以灌賊。

translations.literal: Moreover, ten paces inside the city from the wall, he dug down to the springs, made extensive tunnels, sent hidden troops out through them, set up furnaces to cast iron, and poured it down upon the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He also had tunnels dug ten paces inside the wall down to the water table, sent hidden troops out through them, set up furnaces to melt iron, and poured the molten metal down on the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊遂相語曰：「不畏利槊堅城，唯畏楊公鐵星。

translations.literal: The bandits then said to one another, "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls—only Lord Yang's iron stars."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then said among themselves, "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls—we fear only Lord Yang's iron stars."

sentences.zh: 」津與賊帥元洪業及與賊中督將尉靈根、程殺鬼、潘法顯等書，曉喻之，并授鐵券，許以爵位，令圖賊帥毛普賢。

translations.literal: Jin wrote to the bandit chief Yuan Hongye and to the bandits' supervising generals Wei Linggen, Cheng Shagui, Pan Faxian, and others, instructing them, and also gave them iron covenants, promising them noble rank and ordering them to plot against the bandit chief Mao Puxian.
translations.idiomatic: Jin wrote to the bandit chief Yuan Hongye and to the rebel supervising generals Wei Linggen, Cheng Shagui, Pan Faxian, and others, urging them to come over. He also gave them iron covenants, promised them noble rank, and instructed them to plot against the bandit chief Mao Puxian.

sentences.zh: 洪業等感悟，復書云：「今與諸人密議，欲殺普賢，願公聽之。

translations.literal: Hongye and the others were moved and replied, "We are now in secret consultation with the others and wish to kill Puxian; we ask that you approve."
translations.idiomatic: Hongye and the others were persuaded and wrote back, "We are now in secret consultation with the others and plan to kill Puxian; we ask that you approve."

sentences.zh: 又賊欲圍城，正為取北人耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, the bandits wish to besiege the city precisely in order to seize the northerners.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the bandits mean to besiege the city precisely in order to seize the northerners within it.

sentences.zh: 城中所有北人，必須盡殺，公若置之，恐縱敵為患矣。

translations.literal: All the northerners in the city must be killed entirely; if you spare them, I fear you will release enemies and create a future threat.
translations.idiomatic: All the northerners in the city must be killed; if you spare them, I fear you will be nurturing enemies and creating a future threat.

sentences.zh: 願公察之。

translations.literal: I ask that you consider this.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」津以城內北人雖是惡黨，然掌握中物，未忍便殺，但收內子城防禁而已。

translations.literal: Jin reasoned that although the northerners in the city were a wicked faction, they still held things in their grasp, and he could not bear to kill them outright; he only gathered them into the inner city and placed them under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jin reasoned that although the northerners in the city were a dangerous faction, they still held leverage, and he could not bring himself to kill them outright. He only gathered them into the inner city and placed them under guard.

sentences.zh: 將吏無不感其仁恕。

translations.literal: None of the officers and clerks failed to be moved by his benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer and clerk was moved by his benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初以鐵券二十枚委津分給，津隨賊中首領，間行送之，脩禮、普賢頗亦由此而死。

translations.literal: The court had initially entrusted Jin with twenty iron covenants to distribute; Jin sent them secretly by hidden routes according to the bandit chiefs, and Xiuli and Puxian largely died because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The court had initially entrusted Jin with twenty iron covenants to distribute. He sent them by secret routes to bandit leaders within the enemy ranks, and Xiuli and Puxian largely met their deaths because of this.

sentences.zh: 既而，杜洛周圍州城，津盡力捍守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin defended it with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin defended it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 詔加衞將軍，封開國縣侯，邑一千戶，將士有功者任津科賞，兵民給復八年。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to General of the Guard, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Kaiguo with a fief of one thousand households, authorized Jin to reward meritorious officers and soldiers, and granted soldiers and civilians eight years' exemption from taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to General of the Guard, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Kaiguo with a fief of one thousand households, authorized Jin to reward meritorious officers and soldiers as he saw fit, and granted soldiers and civilians an eight-year exemption from taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 葛榮以司徒說津，津大怒，斬其使以絕之。

translations.literal: Ge Rong tried to win Jin over with the offer of Minister of Works; Jin was greatly angered, beheaded the envoy, and broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong tried to win Jin over with the promise of the post of Minister of Works. Jin was furious, beheaded the envoy, and broke off all contact.

sentences.zh: 自受攻圍，經涉三稔，朝廷不能拯赴。

translations.literal: From the time he came under siege, three full years passed, and the court could not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the siege began, three full years passed without the court being able to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 乃遣長子遁突圍而出，詣蠕蠕主阿那瓌，令其討賊。

translations.literal: He then sent his eldest son Dun to break out of the encirclement, go to the Rouran ruler Anagui, and ask him to campaign against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his eldest son Dun to break through the siege, go to the Rouran ruler Anagui, and ask him to campaign against the bandits.

sentences.zh: 遁日夜泣論，阿那瓌遣其從祖吐豆發率精騎一萬南出，前鋒已達廣昌，賊防塞隘口，蠕蠕持疑，遂還。

translations.literal: Dun pleaded day and night with tears; Anagui sent his collateral ancestor Tudufa at the head of ten thousand elite horsemen south; the vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the bandits blocked the passes, the Rouran hesitated, and they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Dun pleaded day and night with tears. Anagui sent his collateral kinsman Tudufa at the head of ten thousand elite horsemen south. The vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the bandits blocked the passes, the Rouran hesitated, and they turned back.

sentences.zh: 津長史李裔引賊踰城。

translations.literal: Jin's chief clerk Li Yi led the bandits over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's chief clerk Li Yi led the bandits over the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊入轉眾，津苦戰不敵，遂見拘執。

translations.literal: As the bandits entered their numbers grew; Jin fought bitterly but could not prevail and was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: As the bandits poured in their numbers swelled. Jin fought bitterly but could not prevail and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 洛周脫津衣服，置地牢下，數日，欲將烹之，諸賊還相諫止，遂得免害。

translations.literal: Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes and placed him in a dungeon; after several days he intended to boil him alive, but the bandits in turn remonstrated with one another and stopped it, and Jin thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes and threw him into a dungeon. After several days he intended to boil him alive, but the bandits remonstrated with one another and stopped it, and Jin thus escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 津曾與裔相見，對諸賊帥以大義責之，辭淚俱發，裔大慚。

translations.literal: Jin once met Yi and, facing the bandit chiefs, rebuked him on grounds of righteousness; words and tears flowed together, and Yi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once met Yi and, before the bandit chiefs, rebuked him on grounds of righteousness. Words and tears flowed together, and Yi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 典守者以相告，洛周弗之責也。

translations.literal: The custodian reported this to Luozhou, but Luozhou did not hold it against him.
translations.idiomatic: The custodian reported this to Luozhou, but Luozhou did not blame Jin for it.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮吞洛周，復為榮所拘守，榮破，始得還洛。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong swallowed up Luozhou, Jin was again held captive by Rong; when Rong was defeated, he was finally able to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou's forces, Jin was again held captive by Rong. After Rong's defeat he was finally able to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 永安初，詔除津本將軍、荊州刺史，加散騎常侍、當州都督。

translations.literal: Early in Yong'an an edict appointed Jin to his former generalship and Governor of Jingzhou, with the additional titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Commander of that province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yong'an an edict appointed Jin to his former generalship and the governorship of Jingzhou, with the additional titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and commander of that province.

sentences.zh: 津以前在中山陷寇，詣闕固辭，竟不之任。

translations.literal: Jin, having previously fallen captive to bandits at Zhongshan, went to court and firmly declined, and in the end did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, having previously been captured by bandits at Zhongshan, went to court and firmly declined the post, and in the end never took it up.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼吏部尚書，又除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫，仍除吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year he served concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing, was then appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Master of Left Splendid Happiness, and was again appointed to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing, was then appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Master of Left Splendid Happiness, and was again appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 元顥內逼，莊帝將親出討，以津為中軍大都督、兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao pressed from within, and Emperor Zhuang was about to go out in person to campaign against him; Jin was made Grand Commander of the Central Army and concurrent General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed the capital from within, Emperor Zhuang was about to go out in person to campaign against him. Jin was made Grand Commander of the Central Army and concurrent General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 未行，顥入。

translations.literal: Before he marched, Hao entered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor could march, Hao entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 及顥敗，津乃入宿殿中，掃洒宮掖，遣第二子逸封閉府庫，各令防守。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Jin then entered and lodged in the palace halls, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, and sent his second son Yi to seal the treasuries and assign guards to each.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, Jin entered the palace, lodged in the halls, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, and sent his second son Yi to seal the treasuries and assign guards to each.

sentences.zh: 及帝入也，津迎於北邙，流涕謝罪，帝深嘉慰之。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered, Jin met him at Beimang, wept and asked forgiveness, and the emperor greatly praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Jin met him at Beimang, wept and asked forgiveness, and the emperor greatly praised and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 尋以津為司空、加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon Jin was made Minister of Works with the additional title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin was appointed Minister of Works with the additional title Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 長子遁，字山才。

translations.literal: His eldest son Dun, styled Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Dun, whose style name was Shancai.

sentences.zh: 其家貴顯，諸子弱冠，咸縻王爵，而遁性澹退，年近三十，方為鎮西府主簿。

translations.literal: His family was noble and eminent; when the sons reached maturity they all received princely titles, but Dun's nature was calm and retiring, and only near age thirty did he become chief clerk of the Western Pacification headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His family was noble and eminent; when the sons came of age they all received princely titles, but Dun's nature was calm and retiring, and only near the age of thirty did he become chief clerk on the staff of the Western Pacification headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to master of writing.

sentences.zh: 莊帝北巡，奉詔慰勞山東。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang toured the north, Dun received an edict to comfort and reward the eastern mountains region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang toured the north, Dun received an edict to comfort and reward the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 車駕入洛，除尚書左丞，又為光祿大夫，仍左丞。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, he was appointed Left Director of the Masters of Writing, then made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness while retaining the left directorship.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, he was appointed Left Director of the Masters of Writing, then promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness while retaining the left directorship.

sentences.zh: 永安末，父津受委河北，兼黃門郎詣鄴，參行省事，尋遷征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Late in Yong'an his father Jin was entrusted with Hebei, and Dun concurrently served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and went to Ye to assist in administrative affairs; soon he was promoted to General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yong'an his father Jin was entrusted with Hebei. Dun concurrently served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and went to Ye to assist in administrative affairs; soon he was promoted to General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 亦被害於洛，時年四十二。

translations.literal: He too was killed at Luoyang, at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed at Luoyang, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史，諡曰恭定。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was posthumously granted Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Youzhou, and was given the posthumous epithet Gongding.

sentences.zh: 遁弟逸，字遵道，有當世才度。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Yi, styled Zundao, had talent and capacity for his age.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Yi, whose style name was Zundao, possessed talent and stature suited to his age.

sentences.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Supernumerary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as supernumerary attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵華陰男，轉給事中。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Baron of Huayin and transferred to Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted the title Baron of Huayin and transferred to attendant within the gates.

sentences.zh: 父津在中山，為賊攻逼，逸請使於尒朱榮，徵師赴救，詔許之。

translations.literal: When his father Jin was at Zhongshan and pressed by bandits, Yi requested to go as envoy to Erzhu Rong to summon troops for relief, and an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Jin was besieged by bandits at Zhongshan, Yi requested permission to go as envoy to Erzhu Rong to summon relief troops, and an edict approved the mission.

sentences.zh: 建義初，莊帝猶在河陽，逸獨往謁，帝特除給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyi Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang; Yi went alone to pay his respects, and the emperor specially appointed him Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and concurrent Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyi Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang. Yi went alone to pay his respects, and the emperor specially appointed him Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate with concurrent duty as secretariat drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 及朝士濫禍，帝益憂怖，詔逸晝夜陪侍，數日之內，常寢宿於御床前。

translations.literal: When court officials were slaughtered indiscriminately, the emperor grew ever more fearful; an edict ordered Yi to attend day and night, and within several days he often slept before the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials were being slaughtered indiscriminately, the emperor grew ever more fearful. An edict ordered Yi to attend him day and night, and for several days he often slept beside the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 帝曾夜中謂逸曰：「昨來，舉目唯見異人，賴得卿，差以自慰。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Yi in the night, "Of late, wherever I look I see only strange men; thanks to you I am somewhat consoled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Yi in the night, "Of late, wherever I look I see only strange faces; thanks to you I am somewhat consoled."

sentences.zh: 尋除吏部郎中，出為平西將軍、南秦州刺史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Master of Writing in the Ministry of Personnel, sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Nanqinzhou, with the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed master of writing in the Ministry of Personnel, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Nanqinzhou with the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時年二十九，於時方伯之少未有先之者。

translations.literal: At the time he was twenty-nine; among the regional governors of that day, none so young had preceded him.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-nine years old at the time, and among the regional governors of the age, none so young had risen before him.

sentences.zh: 仍以路阻不行，改除平東將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: Still, because the roads were blocked he did not go; his appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roads were impassable, he could not take up his post; his appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 逸折節綏撫，乃心民務，或日昃不食，夜分不寢。

translations.literal: Yi moderated his manner to soothe and comfort the people, devoting his heart to the people's affairs; at times he would not eat when the sun slanted west, and at midnight would not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Yi lowered himself to soothe and comfort the people, giving his whole heart to public affairs; sometimes he skipped eating even when the sun was past noon, and at midnight he still would not sleep.

sentences.zh: 至於兵人從役，必親自送之，或風日之中，雨雪之下，人不堪其勞，逸曾無倦色。

translations.literal: As for soldiers on corvée, he always saw them off in person; at times amid wind and sun, or under rain and snow, others could not bear the hardship, yet Yi never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers set out for corvée duty, he always saw them off in person; even in blazing wind and sun or driving rain and snow, when others could not bear the hardship, Yi never showed a trace of weariness.

sentences.zh: 又法令嚴明，寬猛相濟，於是合境肅然，莫敢干犯。

translations.literal: Moreover his laws and ordinances were strict and clear, leniency and severity complementing each other; thus the whole jurisdiction became orderly, and none dared to violate them.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were strict and clear, and leniency and severity worked together; the whole prefecture became orderly, and no one dared break them.

sentences.zh: 時災儉連歲，人多餓死，逸欲以倉粟賑給，而所司懼罪不敢。

translations.literal: In those years famine followed disaster year after year, and many died of starvation. Yi wished to give out grain from the granaries to relieve them, but the officials in charge feared punishment and did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck year after year, and many people starved to death. Yi wished to distribute grain from the public granaries to relieve them, but the officials in charge feared punishment and did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 逸曰：「國以人為本，人以食為命，百姓不足，君孰與足？

translations.literal: Yi said, "The state takes people as its foundation; people take food as their life. If the common people are not provided for, with whom will the ruler be provided?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The state takes people as its foundation, and people take food as their life. If the common people have not enough, how can the ruler have enough?"

sentences.zh: 假令以此獲戾，吾所甘心。

translations.literal: Even if I should incur guilt on this account, I accept it willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I should incur guilt for this, I accept it willingly.

sentences.zh: 」遂出粟，然後申表。

translations.literal: " So he gave out the grain, then submitted his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " He released the grain, then submitted his memorial afterward.

sentences.zh: 右僕射元羅以下謂公儲難闕，並執不許。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yuan Luo and those below him said the public stores could hardly be depleted, and all held firm in not approving.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yuan Luo and others argued that the public stores could not be depleted, and all opposed the move.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、臨淮王彧以為宜貸二萬。

translations.literal: Minister Over the Masters of Writing, Prince Huai of Linhuai Yu, held that twenty thousand should be loaned.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Over the Masters of Writing, Prince Huai of Linhuai Yu, held that twenty thousand should be lent out.

sentences.zh: 詔聽二萬。

translations.literal: An edict approved twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the loan of twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: [9]逸既出粟之後，其老小殘疾不能自存活者，又於州門煮粥飯之，將死而得濟者以萬數。

translations.literal: [9] After Yi had given out grain, for the old and young and disabled who could not support themselves, he also cooked porridge and rice at the prefecture gate to feed them; those on the verge of death who were saved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: [9] After Yi released grain, he also set up porridge kitchens at the prefecture gate to feed the old, the young, and the disabled who could not survive on their own; those on the point of death who were saved numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he approved.

sentences.zh: 逸為政愛人，尤憎豪猾，廣設耳目。

translations.literal: In governing, Yi loved the people and especially hated the powerful and cunning; he widely set up informants.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Yi cared for the people and especially hated the powerful and unscrupulous; he set up informants throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 其兵吏出使下邑，皆自持糧，人或為設食者，雖在闇室，終不進，咸言楊使君有千里眼，那可欺之。

translations.literal: When his military clerks went on missions to subordinate districts, they all carried their own provisions; even if someone prepared food for them, even in a dark room they would not partake, all saying, "Commissioner Yang has eyes that see a thousand li—how could one deceive him?"
translations.idiomatic: When his military clerks went on missions to local districts, they all carried their own provisions; even if someone offered food, even in a dark room they would not accept it. All said, "Commissioner Yang sees a thousand li—how could anyone fool him?"

sentences.zh: 在州政績尤美。

translations.literal: His achievements as governor were especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements as governor were especially outstanding.

sentences.zh: 及其家禍，尒朱仲遠遣使於州害之，時年三十二。

translations.literal: When his family met with disaster, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent an envoy to the province to kill him; he was thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck his family, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent an envoy to the province to kill him, at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 吏人如喪親戚，城邑村落，為營齋供，一月之中，所在不絕。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners mourned as for kin; in town and village they set up offerings and vegetarian feasts, and within a month such rites were continuous everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners mourned as though they had lost kin; in towns and villages they set up offerings and vegetarian feasts, and for a month such rites never ceased anywhere.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈都督豫郢二州諸軍事、衞將軍、尚書僕射、豫州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was posthumously granted Grand Commander of military affairs in Yuzhou and Yingzhou, General of the Guard, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yuzhou, with posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored as Grand Commander of military affairs in Yuzhou and Yingzhou, General of the Guard, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yuzhou, and given the posthumous epithet Zhen.

sentences.zh: 逸弟謐，字遵智。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Mi, styled Zunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Mi, whose style name was Zunzhi.

sentences.zh: 辟太尉行參軍，歷員外散騎常侍，以功賜爵弘農伯、鎮軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as an aide on the Grand Marshal's staff, served successively as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and for merit was granted the title Baron of Hongnong, General Who Stabilizes the Army, Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as aide on the grand marshal's staff, rose through successive posts to supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and for merit was granted the title Baron of Hongnong, General Who Stabilizes the Army, Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 在晉陽，為尒朱兆所害。

translations.literal: At Jinyang he was killed by Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he was killed by Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈驃騎將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was posthumously granted Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was posthumously honored as Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 謐弟遵彥，武定中，吏部尚書、華陰縣開國侯。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Zunyan; during Wuding he was Minister of Personnel and Marquis Who Founded the State of Huayin County.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Zunyan served during the Wuding era as Minister of Personnel and Marquis Who Founded the State of Huayin County.

sentences.zh: 津弟暐，字延季。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Wei, styled Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Wei, whose style name was Yanji.

sentences.zh: 性雅厚，頗有文學。

translations.literal: His nature was refined and generous, and he had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was refined and generous by nature, with considerable literary learning.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，稍遷散騎侍郎、直閤將軍、本州大中正、兼武衞將軍、尚食典御。

translations.literal: He began his career as a palace attendant, then was gradually promoted to attendant of the scattered cavalry, general of the palace gate guard, senior selector of his native prefecture, concurrent general of the martial guard, and director of the imperial food service.
translations.idiomatic: He began as palace attendant and was gradually promoted through attendant of the scattered cavalry, general of the palace gate guard, senior selector of his native prefecture, concurrent general of the martial guard, and director of the imperial food service.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，正武衞將軍，加散騎常侍、安南將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaochang he was made regular general of the martial guard, with the additional titles regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang he became regular general of the martial guard, with the additional titles regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害於河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈衞將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of the Guard, honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Guard, with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子元讓，武定末，尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Yuanrang; late in Wuding he was director in the Ministry of Rites of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanrang served late in Wuding as director in the Ministry of Rites of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 播家世純厚，並敦義讓，昆季相事，有如父子。

translations.literal: Bo's family had long been pure and generous; all cultivated righteousness and deference; the brothers served one another like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's clan had long been pure and generous; all cultivated righteousness and deference; the brothers treated one another like father and son.

sentences.zh: 播剛毅。

translations.literal: Bo was resolute and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was resolute and firm in character.

sentences.zh: 椿、津恭謙，與人言，自稱名字。

translations.literal: Chun and Jin were respectful and modest; when speaking with others they called themselves by their personal names.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Jin were respectful and modest; when speaking to others they used their own personal names.

sentences.zh: 兄弟旦則聚於廳堂，終日相對，未曾入內。

translations.literal: The brothers gathered in the hall each morning and faced one another all day, never going inside to the women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning the brothers gathered in the hall and sat facing one another all day, never retreating to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 有一美味，不集不食。

translations.literal: When there was a fine delicacy, they would not eat unless all were assembled.
translations.idiomatic: No fine dish was eaten unless all were gathered together.

sentences.zh: 廳堂間，往往幃幔隔障，為寢息之所，時就休偃，還共談笑。

translations.literal: Within the hall, curtains and screens were often hung as partitions to make places for rest; at times they would go to lie down, then return and talk and laugh together.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains and screens often divided spaces within the hall for resting; when they needed to lie down they did so there, then returned to talk and laugh together.

sentences.zh: 椿年老，曾他處醉歸，津扶侍還室，仍假寐閤前，承候安否。

translations.literal: Chun was elderly; once when he returned drunk from elsewhere, Jin supported him back to his room, then feigned sleep before his door to await word whether he was well.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was growing old. Once when he returned drunk from elsewhere, Jin supported him to his room, then pretended to sleep before his door to await word whether he was well.

sentences.zh: 椿、津年過六十，並登台鼎，而津嘗旦暮參問，子姪羅列階下，椿不命坐，津不敢坐。

translations.literal: Chun and Jin passed sixty years of age, both reaching the highest offices, yet Jin would attend morning and evening to pay his respects; when nephews and sons lined the steps below, Chun would not command him to sit, and Jin did not dare sit.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Jin were both past sixty and had reached the highest offices, yet Jin still paid morning and evening respects; with sons and nephews lined up on the steps below, Chun would not tell Jin to sit, and Jin did not dare sit.

sentences.zh: 椿每近出，或日斜不至，津不先飯，椿還，然後共食。

translations.literal: Whenever Chun went out nearby, if at sunset he had not returned, Jin would not eat first; only when Chun returned would they eat together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chun went out nearby, if he had not returned by sunset Jin would not eat first; only after Chun returned would they eat together.

sentences.zh: 食則津親授匙箸，味皆先嘗，椿命食，然後食。

translations.literal: At meals Jin would personally hand him spoon and chopsticks; every dish he tasted first, and only when Chun commanded him to eat would he eat.
translations.idiomatic: At meals Jin personally handed him spoon and chopsticks, tasted every dish first, and only ate when Chun told him to.

sentences.zh: 津為司空，於時府主皆引僚佐，人就津求官，津曰：「此事須家兄裁之，何為見問？

translations.literal: When Jin was Minister of Works, the heads of offices at the time all brought in staff officers; people came to Jin seeking office. Jin said, "This matter requires my elder brother's decision—why ask me?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was Minister of Works, office heads brought in their staff as custom dictated; people came to Jin seeking appointments. Jin said, "This requires my elder brother's decision—why ask me?"

sentences.zh: 」初，津為肆州，椿在京宅，每有四時嘉味，輒因使次附之，若或未寄，不先入口。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Jin was in Sizhou and Chun was at the capital residence, whenever there were fine seasonal delicacies, he would always send them along with a courier; if none had been sent, he would not put them in his mouth first.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when Jin was governor of Sizhou and Chun was at the capital residence, whenever there were fine seasonal delicacies Jin would send them along with the next courier; if none had been sent, he would not taste them first.

sentences.zh: 椿每得所寄，輒對之下泣。

translations.literal: Whenever Chun received what was sent, he would weep over it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chun received what Jin sent, he would weep over it.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆有孫，唯椿有曾孫，年十五六矣，椿常欲為之早娶，望見玄孫。

translations.literal: All the brothers had grandsons; only Chun had a great-grandson, fifteen or sixteen years old; Chun often wished to marry him early, hoping to see a great-great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: All the brothers had grandsons; only Chun had a great-grandson, fifteen or sixteen years old. Chun often wanted to marry him early, hoping to live to see a great-great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 自昱已下，率多學尚，時人莫不欽羨焉。

translations.literal: From Yu downward, most were devoted to learning; people of the time all admired and envied them.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu downward, most were devoted to learning, and people of the time all admired and envied them.

sentences.zh: 一家之內，男女百口，緦服同爨，庭無間言，魏世以來，唯有盧淵兄弟及播昆季，當世莫逮焉。

translations.literal: Within one household, men and women numbered a hundred mouths; kin in mourning garments ate from the same hearth, and in the household there was no ill speech. Since the Wei dynasty only the brothers Lu Yuan and Bo's brothers had been so—none in the age could match them.
translations.idiomatic: Within one household, a hundred men and women wore mourning cloth and ate from the same hearth, without a cross word under the roof. Since the Wei dynasty only the brothers Lu Yuan and Bo's brothers had achieved this—none in the age could match them.

sentences.zh: 世隆等將害椿家，誣其為逆，奏請收治。

translations.literal: Shilong and others wished to destroy Chun's family, falsely accused them of rebellion, and memorialized requesting arrest and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and his allies wished to destroy Chun's family, falsely accused them of rebellion, and memorialized requesting their arrest and investigation.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝不許，世隆復苦執，不得已，下詔付有司檢聞。

translations.literal: The Deposed Former Emperor did not consent; Shilong pressed again relentlessly; with no alternative, an edict was issued entrusting the matter to the relevant offices for investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Former Emperor refused, but Shilong pressed again and again; with no alternative, an edict was issued ordering the relevant offices to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 世隆遂遣步騎夜圍其宅，天光亦同日收椿於華陰。

translations.literal: Shilong then sent infantry and cavalry by night to surround their residence; on the same day Tianguang also seized Chun at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong then sent infantry and cavalry by night to surround their residence; on the same day Tianguang seized Chun at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 東西兩家，無少長皆遇禍，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the eastern and western households, none young or old escaped disaster, and their estates were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern and western households, none young or old escaped disaster, and their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 世隆後乃奏云：「楊家實反，夜拒軍人，遂盡格殺。

translations.literal: Only later did Shilong memorialize, saying, "The Yang family truly rebelled; by night they resisted the troops, and so all were killed."
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward did Shilong memorialize: "The Yang family truly rebelled; they resisted the troops by night, and so all were killed."

sentences.zh: 」廢帝惋悵久之，不言而已。

translations.literal: " The Deposed Emperor grieved and lamented for a long time, saying nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: " The Deposed Emperor grieved for a long time and said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 知世隆縱擅，無如之何。

translations.literal: Knowing Shilong's arbitrary excess, he could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Shilong's arbitrary excess, he could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，椿合家歸葬華陰，眾咸觀而悲傷焉。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, Chun's whole household was returned and buried at Huayin; the multitude all witnessed it and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi, Chun's whole household was returned and buried at Huayin; crowds gathered and grieved at the sight.

sentences.zh: 播族弟鈞。

translations.literal: Bo's clansman Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's clansman Jun.

sentences.zh: 祖暉，庫部給事，稍遷洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was a clerk in the Storehouse Section, and was gradually promoted to Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui served as clerk in the Storehouse Section and was gradually promoted to Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈弘農公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously granted Duke of Hongnong, with posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously granted Duke of Hongnong with the posthumous epithet Jian.

sentences.zh: 父恩，河間太守。

translations.literal: His father En was Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His father En was Administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 鈞頗有幹用，自廷尉正為長水校尉、中壘將軍、洛陽令。

translations.literal: Jun had considerable administrative ability; from director in the Court of Justice he became colonel of the Changshui Regiment, general of the central rampart garrison, and magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had considerable administrative ability; from director in the Court of Justice he became colonel of the Changshui Regiment, general of the central rampart garrison, and magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 出除中山太守，入為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed Administrator of Zhongshan, then entered the capital as Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Zhongshan, then recalled to serve as Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 又除徐州、東荊州刺史，還為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Governor of Xuzhou and Eastern Jingzhou, then returned as Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Governor of Xuzhou and Eastern Jingzhou, then returned to serve as Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 拜恒州刺史，轉懷朔鎮將。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Hengzhou, then transferred to be garrison commander of Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Hengzhou, then transferred to garrison commander of Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 所居以強濟稱。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was known for strength and effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he was known for vigor and effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 後為撫軍將軍、七兵尚書、北道行臺。

translations.literal: Later he was General Who Calms the Army, Minister of the Seven Troops, and chief of the North Route mobile office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as General Who Calms the Army, Minister of the Seven Troops, and chief of the North Route mobile office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、華州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously granted the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously granted the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 長子暄，卒於尚書郎。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xuan died while serving as master of writing.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xuan died while serving as master of writing.

sentences.zh: 暄弟穆，華州別駕。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Mu was aide to the Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Mu served as aide to the Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 穆弟儉，寧遠將軍、頓丘太守。

translations.literal: Mu's younger brother Jian was General of Far Pacification and Administrator of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's younger brother Jian was General of Far Pacification and Administrator of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除太府少卿。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyi he was appointed Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyi he was appointed Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 尋為華州中正，加左將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was senior selector of Huazhou with the additional title General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became senior selector of Huazhou with the additional title General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 儉與元顥有舊，及顥入洛，受其位任。

translations.literal: Jian had old ties with Yuan Hao; when Hao entered Luoyang, Jian accepted office from him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had old ties with Yuan Hao; when Hao entered Luoyang, Jian accepted office from him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，坐免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Jian was dismissed for this offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he was dismissed for this offense.

sentences.zh: 後以本將軍潁州刺史，[10]尋加散騎常侍、平南將軍，州罷不行。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Yingzhou with his existing rank as general; [10] soon he was given the additional titles regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South; the prefecture was abolished and he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Governor of Yingzhou at his existing rank as general; [10] soon he was given the additional titles regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South, but the prefecture was abolished and he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Putai he was appointed General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Putai he was appointed General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，以本將軍除北雍州刺史，仍陷關西。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was appointed Governor of Northern Yongzhou at his existing rank as general, and subsequently fell into the western passes.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was appointed Governor of Northern Yongzhou at his existing rank as general, and subsequently fell into captivity west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 儉弟寬，自宗正丞，建義初為通直散騎侍郎，領河南尹丞。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Kuan, from director in the Directorate of Imperial Clans, at the beginning of Jianyi was made unqualified attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent aide to the Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Kuan had served as director in the Directorate of Imperial Clans; at the beginning of Jianyi he was made unqualified attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent aide to the Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 稍遷散騎常侍、安東將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，除中軍將軍、太府卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was appointed General of the Central Army and Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was appointed General of the Central Army and Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、右光祿大夫、澄城縣開國伯。

translations.literal: Later he was regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Baron Who Founded the State of Chengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Baron Who Founded the State of Chengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除給事黃門侍郎，尋加驃騎大將軍，除華州大中正，監內典書事。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was appointed Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; soon he was given the additional title Grand General of Fast Cavalry, appointed senior selector of Huazhou, and put in charge of the imperial library archives.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was appointed Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; soon he was given the additional title Grand General of Fast Cavalry, appointed senior selector of Huazhou, and put in charge of the imperial library archives.

sentences.zh: 坐事去官。

translations.literal: For an offense he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，兼武衞將軍，又除黃門郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was made concurrent general of the martial guard, and again appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was made concurrent general of the martial guard and again appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 隨出帝入關西。

translations.literal: He followed the Outgoing Emperor into the region west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Outgoing Emperor west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 儉、寬皆輕薄無行，為人流所鄙。

translations.literal: Jian and Kuan were both frivolous and without moral conduct; they were despised by people of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Kuan were both frivolous and without moral conduct, and were despised by their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：楊播兄弟，俱以忠毅謙謹，荷內外之任，公卿牧守，榮赫累朝，所謂門生故吏遍於天下。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yang Bo and his brothers were all loyal, resolute, humble, and cautious, bearing duties within and without; as ministers and governors their glory blazed across successive reigns—the so-called disciples and former subordinates spread across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The brothers Yang Bo were all loyal, resolute, humble, and cautious, bearing duties at court and in the provinces; as ministers and governors their glory blazed across successive reigns—the so-called disciples and former subordinates filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 而言色恂恂，出於誠至，恭德慎行，為世師範，漢之萬石家風、陳紀門法，所不過也。

translations.literal: Yet in speech and countenance they were ever deferential, arising from true sincerity; in respectful virtue and careful conduct they were models for the age—the family ethos of the Wanshi in Han and the household discipline of Chen Ji did not exceed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in speech and bearing they were ever deferential, from genuine sincerity; in respectful virtue and careful conduct they were models for the age—the family ethos of the Wanshi in Han and the household discipline of Chen Ji did not surpass them.

sentences.zh: 諸子秀立，青紫盈庭，其積善之慶歟？

translations.literal: Their sons stood forth in excellence, officials' purple and blue filling the halls—is this the reward of accumulated virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Their sons stood forth in excellence, officials' robes filling the hall—is this the reward of accumulated virtue?

sentences.zh: 及胡逆擅朝，淫刑肆毒，以斯族而遇斯禍，報施之理，何相及哉！

translations.literal: When the barbarian rebel monopolized the court and wanton punishments ran riot, this clan met such disaster—what has the principle of retribution to do with it!
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarian rebel monopolized the court and wanton punishments ran riot, this clan met such disaster—what has the principle of retribution to do with it!

translations.literal: According to the biography of Erzhu Rong in juan 74, which narrates this affair: "The various Yangs of Mazhu said they had several small boats and asked to serve as guides; Rong then ordered Erzhu Zhao and others to lead picked cavalry across by night."
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Erzhu Rong in juan 74 recounts this episode: "The Yang clan of Mazhu reported that they had several small boats and offered to act as guides, whereupon Rong ordered Erzhu Zhao and others to lead elite cavalry across the river by night."

translations.idiomatic: The biography of Yang Juan in juan 34 of the Book of Zhou states: "Juan led his kinsmen and collected boats at Mazhu."

sentences.zh: 」馬渚是黃河渡口，楊𢷋族人居於馬渚，故稱他們為「馬渚諸楊」。

translations.literal: Mazhu was a Yellow River crossing; the Yang Juan clan dwelt at Mazhu, hence they were called "the various Yangs of Mazhu."
translations.idiomatic: Mazhu was a ford on the Yellow River where the Yang Juan clan lived, which is why they were called "the Yangs of Mazhu."

sentences.zh: 「諸」字不宜省，「於」是「與」字之訛，今據北史、冊府改補。

translations.idiomatic: The word "various" should not be dropped; "at" is a scribal error for "with," and the present text follows the Northern History and the Prime Tortoise in restoring it.

translations.idiomatic: On "reassigned to the Central Section": in the Northern History biography of Yang Chun appended to Yang Bo, juan 41, the word "law" follows "central."

sentences.zh: 按此官不見卷一一三官氏志。

translations.idiomatic: This office does not appear in the Monograph on Offices, juan 113.

sentences.zh: 魏有內、中、外三都大官，管刑獄事。

translations.literal: Wei had three great directors of the capital—inner, central, and outer—who oversaw penal and prison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had three great capital directors—inner, central, and outer—charged with criminal and prison matters.

sentences.zh: 元宏曾說「三都折獄，特宜慎重」。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong once said, "In the three capitals' adjudication of cases, special care should be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong once remarked that "in the three capitals' handling of cases, exceptional caution is required."

translations.literal: Those who held the office of great director of the central capital, such as Prince Rencheng Yun, Prince Jingzhao Zitui, and Prince Guangchuan Lue, are all mentioned in their basic biographies as handling penal and prison affairs in office.
translations.idiomatic: Men who served as great director of the central capital, such as Princes Yun of Rencheng, Zitui of Jingzhao, and Lue of Guangchuan, are all recorded in their biographies as having administered criminal justice in that post.

sentences.zh: 疑這裏「部」字乃「都」之訛，「中都曹」屬中都大官，所以管獄訟。

translations.idiomatic: It is likely that "section" here is a scribal error for "capital," and that the Central Capital Section belonged to the great director of the central capital and therefore handled lawsuits and imprisonment.

translations.idiomatic: The Northern History adds the word "law" because the text below speaks of "fair adjudication of lawsuits."

translations.idiomatic: Que'ao was then an important stronghold and the administrative seat of Jizhou

translations.idiomatic: The text reads "province" instead of "commandery."

sentences.zh: 按郡不當有刺史，「番州」也不見記載，或臨時設置，續靈珍死後，州名亦廢。

translations.literal: A commandery ought not to have a provincial governor; "Fan province" is also not recorded—it may have been a temporary establishment, and after Xu Lingzhen's death the provincial name was likewise abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery should not have a provincial governor, and "Fan province" is nowhere else recorded; it was probably a temporary designation, abolished after Xu Lingzhen's death.

sentences.zh: 在城東十里被殺 諸本「殺」作「劫」，北史卷四一楊播附楊津傳、御覽卷八一七

translations.literal: Killed ten li east of the city: in various editions "killed" is written as "robbed"; Northern History, biography of Yang Jin appended to Yang Bo, juan 41, and Imperial Readings, juan 817
translations.idiomatic: On "killed ten li east of the city": various editions read "robbed" for "killed"; Northern History, biography of Yang Jin, juan 41, and Imperial Readings, juan 817

sentences.zh: 〈三六三四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3634〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 3634〉

sentences.zh: 作「殺」。

translations.literal: read "killed."
translations.idiomatic: both read "killed."

sentences.zh: 按若說「被劫」，其人現存，豈得云「家人可速收視」。

translations.literal: If it said "was robbed," the man would still be alive—how could one then say "the family may quickly come to attend to him"?
translations.idiomatic: If the text meant "was robbed," the man would still be alive—how then could he tell his family to "come quickly and attend to me"?

sentences.zh: 據御覽，知魏書本亦作「殺」，後人因上文稱「被劫」，以為「殺」字誤，妄改作「劫」，今據北史、御覽回改。

translations.literal: According to the Imperial Readings, the original Book of Wei also read "killed"; later people, because the passage above speaks of "being robbed," thought "killed" was wrong and rashly changed it to "robbed"; it is now restored according to the Northern History and Imperial Readings.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Readings shows that the Book of Wei originally read "killed"; later editors, misled by the earlier mention of robbery, wrongly changed it to "robbed"; the text is restored here on the authority of the Northern History and Imperial Readings.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥薛脩禮 北史卷四一楊播附楊津傳「薛」作「鮮于」。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chief Xue Xiuli: in the biography of Yang Jin appended to Yang Bo in juan 41 of the Northern History, "Xue" is written as "Xianyu."
translations.idiomatic: On "the bandit chief Xue Xiuli": in the Northern History biography of Yang Jin, "Xue" appears as "Xianyu."

sentences.zh: 按「薛脩禮」只此一見，此傳前文和魏書他處記載都只作「鮮于脩禮」，當時攻圍定州的也只有鮮于脩禮和杜洛周兩支起義軍。

translations.literal: "Xue Xiuli" appears only here; earlier in this biography and elsewhere in the Book of Wei the name is only "Xianyu Xiuli," and at that time only the rebel armies of Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou besieged Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: "Xue Xiuli" occurs only here; elsewhere in this biography and in the Book of Wei the rebel is always "Xianyu Xiuli," and only the forces of Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou were then besieging Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雖可能「薛」是「鮮于」所改的漢姓，但別無佐證，且亦不應前後歧異，疑「薛」字誤。

translations.literal: Although it is possible that "Xue" was a sinicized surname adopted by "Xianyu," there is no other corroboration, and the text ought not to differ front and back; "Xue" is suspected to be an error.
translations.idiomatic: Although "Xue" might be a Han surname adopted by the Xianyu clan, there is no supporting evidence, and the name should not vary within one passage; "Xue" is probably a scribal error.

sentences.zh: 詔聽二萬 北史卷四一楊播附楊逸傳「二萬」作「五萬」。

translations.literal: The edict approved twenty thousand: in the biography of Yang Yi appended to Yang Bo in juan 41 of the Northern History, "twenty thousand" is written as "fifty thousand."
translations.idiomatic: On "the edict approved twenty thousand": in the Northern History biography of Yang Yi, "twenty thousand" reads "fifty thousand."

sentences.zh: 按上文稱「尚書令、臨淮王彧以為宜貸二萬」。

translations.literal: The passage above states, "Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince Huaihuai Yu, held that twenty thousand should be lent."
translations.idiomatic: The passage above states that Director Yu, Prince of Huaihuai, recommended lending twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 若「詔聽二萬」，應云「從之」，不必又舉數字。

translations.literal: If the edict approved twenty thousand, it should simply say "followed him," without repeating the figure.
translations.idiomatic: If the edict approved twenty thousand, it should simply say "approved," without repeating the amount.

sentences.zh: 「二」當是「五」之訛。

translations.literal: "Two" should be a corruption of "five."
translations.idiomatic: "Two" is probably a scribal error for "five."

sentences.zh: 後以本將軍潁州刺史 按「將軍」下當脫「除」或「為」字。

translations.literal: Later, with his former general's rank, Governor of Yingzhou: after "general" the characters "appointed" or "as" are probably missing.
translations.idiomatic: On "later, with his former general's rank, Governor of Yingzhou": the words "appointed" or "as" are probably missing after "general."
